column36: Closing the Northern Gap: Stakeholder Perspectives on an eHealth App for Maternal Mental Health in Northwestern Ontario
column37: Women living in Northwestern Ontario (NWO) face many unique barriers in accessing healthcare when compared to those living outside of the North. Peri- and Postpartum depression affects women almost twice as much as men, suicide is the leading cause of death among pregnant women, and hospitalizations for mental health and self-injury in NWO are double the national rate. Yet, There is still a significant gap in access to maternal care and mental health services in NWO. This study will address this gap by exploring the suitability of an eHealth intervention for mothers with peri- and postnatal depression. Therapist-Assisted Internet-delivered Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (TA-ICBT) is an eHealth tool that can be used as a mobile 'app' to match patients with trained therapists, provide online self-management videos, and recommend services to best meet patients' needs. Because TA-ICBT can be delivered remotely, it has the potential to overcome many of the common barriers faced by women in the North. Twenty interviews and four focus groups will be conducted in order to understand what physicians, nurses, and other care providers perceive as key barriers and enablers to using a TA-ICBT app in NWO. This information will be used to adapt the app to best serve our target population. This research will be overseen by an interdisciplinary team of women who have been collecting data on the maternal health in NWO over the past five years. The aim of this study is to inform the future design, development, and delivery of a new TA-ICBT app for women in NWO. This research will be a foundation from which a new healthcare option can be developed to meet the specific needs of women in NWO, and will help close the Northern gap in maternal mental health services.

column36: Altered cortisol reactivity to stress: A potential mediator between adverse childhood experiences and substance use disorders in young adults
column37: Extensive literature has emerged suggesting isolated relationships between three factors. First, a relationship between adverse childhood experiences (ACE) and the development of addictive behaviours during emerging adulthood has been proposed. Second, increasing evidence indicates a link between a history of ACE and altered cortisol reactivity. A third trend has been revealed such that blunted cortisol reactivity has been found in individuals with addictions and substance use disorders. Based on these overall findings, I plan to investigate the role of attenuated cortisol reactivity to stress as a mediator between ACE and the subsequent development of addiction. To do this, I plan to recruit 200 emerging adults (age 18 to 26) with a diagnosis of an addiction or substance use disorder. Half of the individuals included in the study will have a history of childhood adversity based on criteria adapted from the Adverse Childhood Experiences Questionnaire, while the other half will not. All study participants will participate in a mildly stressful challenge, the Trier Social Stress Test. Prior to receiving any information about the stress test and immediately before commencing the task, baseline salivary cortisol samples will be collected. Additional cortisol samples will be collected at five post-stressor time points. The findings from the proposed model will inform new treatment approaches for addiction. Using a Research Domain Criteria (RDoC) approach, we could tailor treatments specifically to clinical populations with a history of ACE, blunted cortisol reactivity and addiction. This theoretical treatment framework could target proximal factors such as maladaptive coping with stress, in the hope of improving treatment outcomes within this identified clinical subgroup.

column36: The influence of apolipoprotein E4 on microglial activity in cervical spondylotic myelopathy
column37: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM) is a devastating neurological condition resulting from the degeneration of spinal structures and the subsequent compression of the spinal cord. CSM is the most common cause of spinal cord dysfunction among adults (>55 years), and can result in severe sensory and motor deficits. Individuals carrying the apolipoprotein E4 (ApoE4) allele have a 77.8% greater risk of developing CSM, and have worse neurological outcomes following surgical treatment. While the role of ApoE4 in CSM pathology is currently unknown, recent evidence suggests that ApoE acts as a ligand for a crucial microglial receptor complex: Triggering Receptor Expressed on Myeloid Cells 2 (TREM2) and DNAX-activating protein 12 (DAP12). Microglia are the innate immune cells of the central nervous system, and inflammatory activation of microglia results in the release of nitric oxide, cytokines, and proteases that can lead to neurotoxicity. Given that activated microglia are known to participate in CSM spinal cord pathology, I hypothesize that the ApoE4 isoform exacerbates CSM progression by promoting a pro-inflammatory microglial phenotype, specifically through interaction with the TREM2-DAP12 complex. The proposed study will focus on the following goals: (1) investigate the neuroinflammatory role ApoE4 and the TREM2-DAP12 complex has on CSM and (2) determine whether inhibition of TREM2-DAP12 signaling can mitigate the negative effect of ApoE4 on the complex in the diseased state. This proposal is the first to investigate the role of ApoE4 in CSM neuroinflammatory mechanisms and experimentally link ApoE4 expression to neurological outcomes in CSM. It will also provide proof-of-concept for a novel personalized medicine strategy to treat an at-risk ApoE4+ CSM population.

column36: Individual Level Prediction of Cognitive Decline in Alzheimer's Disease
column37: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disease with an immense burden on society. A 2017 estimate showed that AD affects over 5 million individuals in the U.S. alone and costs over $200 billions. While no cure has been found, early-detection of AD help with in early-intervention which improves the patients' quality of life and reduces the cost to society. For this reason, individual-level prediction of AD is essential. As it stands, current AD research has identified numerous group-level differences between AD and non-AD subjects, but no robust subject-level detection system is available. This is the problem I would like to solve. Specifically, I will be attempting to predict the decline in cognitive abilities experienced by patients suffering from AD, using machine learning methodologies. I will use unsupervised clustering to identify groups of patients who has similar cognitive trajectories across time (e.g. one group may maintain a high degree of cognitive abilities as they age, while another may show rapid decline). Importantly, I will be extending upon previous works done in the lab to include many different clinical rating scales to provide a nuanced measure of each individual's cognitive ability. Then, I will borrow methods from supervised machine learning to predict which trajectory each subject belongs to, using data that can be collected in the clinic, such as demography, genetics and neuroanatomical structures. This work holds the promise of constructing a robust predictive algorithm which can help clinicians be more informed and make better clinical decisions with regard to the treatment of AD patients.

column36: An aggregate algorithmic approach to prioritizing HIV-1 transmission clusters
column37: For the 37 million people infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), treatment can increase length and quality of life, and prevent transmission to uninfected people. However, over 40% of infected people do not have access to treatment and 1.8 million infections still occur each year. Making sure public health resources can quickly reach people with HIV is important in helping them get treatment that will let them live longer, better lives and prevent the spread of infection. Right now, public health agencies can use HIV DNA samples collected from infected people to identify groups that are transmitting HIV at a high rate. However, this type of approach does not define which group of people needs public health attention most. Adding medical and personal information about the people in high-transmission groups to this method could help determine which group needs targeted attention. Current methods also do not use information about the uninfected people who interact with the people in high-transmission groups, even though their characteristics may affect the rate of HIV transmission. I propose to develop a new method that will identify groups of people who are transmitting HIV at a high rate and determine which of these groups needs public health attention most. First, I will establish an improved method of identifying high-transmission groups based on HIV DNA samples. Next, I will create a computer algorithm that will combine medical and personal information from the people in high-transmission groups together with personal information from the uninfected people they interact with. The algorithm will calculate a score that will rank high-transmission groups by need for public health resources, so that these resources can be used in the best way possible.

column36: A real-time imaging approach to alleviate pain sensation.
column37: My goal is to design a real-time magnetoencephalography imaging approach (rtMEG) to reduce the sensation of pain. Recent evidence from my host lab shows a slowing of brain rhythms in the alpha frequency range (8-12 Hz) in a distributed network of brain regions in chronic pain patients. Based on this finding, I will use MEG real-time source imaging to first refine the definition of neurophysiological markers of the sensation of pain. I will proceed in a controlled experimental design, with tonic heat pain induced in healthy subjects. These signal markers of pain will then be used in a rtMEG feedback loop to train participants to augment their alpha frequencies in targeted regions. We hypothesize this will contribute to reduce their pain sensation. By providing real-time objective feedback reflecting brain activity changes in specific brain oscillatory patterns and anatomical areas, the technology overcomes the limitations of poor spatial resolution of real-time EEG technology. If the proposed rtMEG neurofeedback approach successfully reduces the pain perception in experimental pain, it will be extended to chronic pain to verify its therapeutic efficacy.

column36: Remote Ischemic Post-Conditioning in Patients with Traumatic Brain Injury: A Prospective Randomized Control Trial
column37: Traumatic brain injury (TBI), an impact to the brain caused by an external force, is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in victims of blunt trauma. In 2010, Statistics Canada reported that 133,812 people had sustained a brain injury in the household population. Additionally, incidence numbers are projected to increase by 28% over the next 20 years, according to a 2014 Public Health Agency of Canada report. Due to the complexity introduced by TBI, many conventional approaches fall short. Currently, the management of TBI largely focuses on prevention or reduction of secondary consequences which occur hours to days later from the initial trauma and play a major role in a poor prognosis, which may entail long-term cognitive impairment. To counteract this, it is crucial to support brain circulation, reduce intracranial (i.e. within the skull) fluid retention, and/or decrease metabolic activity during periods of elevated intracranial pressure. Thus, we propose using the low-cost non-invasive Remote Ischemic Conditioning (RIC) procedure. RIC is inducing brief periods of restricted blood flow via a blood pressure cuff at a limb. RIC then elicits inborn systemic protection in distant organs, hence, minimizing subsequent trauma. Research in RIC has shown its benefits to other organs such as the heart and kidneys and at a molecular level in TBI. In this human study, we plan to examine RIC benefits in severe TBI patients by measuring several factors such as brain inflammation markers, brain circulation via imaging technology, and finally, overall cognitive improvement. The implementation of this simple procedure may significantly improve TBI patient outcome and we hope the findings of this study will promote RIC research in other neurological conditions.

column36: Isolation and Characterization of Donor-Derived Exosomes in Human Lung Transplantation
column37: Although lung transplantation is the best strategy for the treatment of patients with lung failure, post-transplant survival is limited to a median of 6 years. This is largely due to the development of chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD), a condition resulting from the body's attack on the foreign donor lung. Because current treatment strategies for CLAD are minimally effective and are associated with numerous side effects, there is need for better therapeutic options. To resolve this need, my study aims at enhancing our understanding of the mechanism underlying the development of CLAD through the analysis of exosomes. Exosomes are small fluid-filled sacs released by most cells of the body. They contain proteins and other molecules that carry information from their cell of origin to neighboring cells. In particular, immune cells responsible for fighting off bacteria and foreign objects in the body release exosomes containing proteins involved in immune activation. This activation could in turn increase the production of exosomes, thus perpetuating injury. Therefore, I predict that exosomes released by donor lungs are present in recipients, and they stimulate immune response which leads to CLAD. To test this, I will isolate and identify donor exosomes from three biological fluids: wash of donor lung outside the body, wash of donor lung after transplantation, and patient's blood. Then, I will analyze the quantity and quality of donor exosomes in each body fluid, and see how these correlate with patient outcome. If CLAD patients present with an altered donor exosome profile compared to stable patients, then this suggests that exosomes may play a role in CLAD development, and treatments strategies may be adjusted accordingly.

column36: Etude des proteines modulant le repliement de motifs G-quadruplexes du transcriptome humain associe a la maladie du Parkinson
column37: Alors qu'on a longtemps cru que la regulation de l'expression genique n'avait lieu principalement qu'au niveau de la transcription de l'ADN, il est desormais etabli que plus de 90% du genome est transcrit en ARN. Ceci a conduit a l'importante demonstration que la regulation post-transcriptionnelle est la pierre angulaire du controle du flot d'information allant du transcriptome vers le proteome. Notre principal interet de recherche est l'etude des G-quadruplexes (G4) d'ARN. Il s'agit de sequences riches en guanosines qui se replient en structures helicoidales a 4 brins non-canoniques. Au cours des dernieres annees notre groupe de recherche a pris le leadership sur la caracterisation des motifs G4 d'ARN en developpant une approche robuste integrant a la fois des experiences in silico, in vitro et in cellulo. Ces travaux ont conduit a la demonstration que certains motifs G4, situes dans les regions 5'- et 3'-UTR d'ARNm humain (et tres souvent associe au developpement de maladies), etaient essentiels a la regulation de la traduction, de la polyadenylation et de la liaison ou non de microARN (miARN) a de nombreux ARNm ainsi qu'a la regulation de la maturation des precurseurs de microARN. Il n'en demeure pas moins que l'etude des G4 d'ARN est encore a ses premiers balbutiements. Les dernieres etudes montrent que ces structures seraient d'une tres grande importance dans les maladies neurodegeneratives. Il est clair que l'identification et l'etude des RBPs (RNA binding proteins) qui facilitent la formation des G4 ou qui les deplient (helicase) est de premiere importance pour reussir faire face a ces maladies. C'est dans cet effort que s'inscrit mon projet de recherche.

column36: Are Connectivity Differences Unique to Pedophilia?
column37: The study I will be completing during my Master's degree is entitled "Are Connectivity Differences Unique to Pedophilia?". The overarching goal of this research is to gain a better understanding of functional (i.e. how the brain actively processes information) and connective (i.e. how different parts of the brain are connected to each other) differences in the neural framework of pedophiles, fetishistic individuals, and non-paraphilic controls with a combination of neuroimaging and behavioural measures. This will be done using structural imaging (including Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI)) and functional MRI. Paraphilia is a condition characterized by intense and persistent abnormal sexual interests and desires (ex. fetishes). Pedophilia, on the other hand, is a specific paraphilia characterized by recurrent, intense, and persistent sexual interest in prepubescent children. The threatening nature of pedophilia and its risk to children make it of great clinical and forensic importance. We hypothesize that our study will reveal significant neural differences in white matter that are unique to pedophilia. The most novel contribution of the proposed research is that our study can reveal whether previously identified neural differences between pedophiles and controls are distinctive of pedophilia or if they are found in other paraphilias, namely foot fetishists. The results of this comparison would determine if existing research reveals a distinctive "brainprint" associated with pedophilia, with implications for etiology and diagnosis. This important difference would also lay the groundwork for a new line of research on the neuroimaging of paraphilias and contribute to our understanding of the neural factors underlying pedophilia.

column36: The effects of exercise and inflammation on neuropathic pain in individuals with a spinal cord injury.
column37: Neuropathic pain (NP) is self-reported as the most severe type of pain following a traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) and places the largest burden on the healthcare system compared to all other types of pain. Although most treatment options for NP are pharmaceutical interventions, this line of treatment only addresses the symptoms rather than the cause of NP. Promising research has shown that exercise can also reduce NP although the mechanism by which this occurs is unknown. One proposed explanation is that exercise reduces inflammation which in turn reduces NP. Under normal circumstances, the inflammatory response is a healthy way for the body to be made aware of acute injurious stimuli and respond accordingly. However, in individuals with SCI, evidence suggests that nervous system impairments can lead to the dysregulation of both endocrine and immune function which can lead to a chronic low-grade inflammation. This chronic low-grade inflammation has been linked to a variety of negative health problems. This study attempts to use exercise to reduce inflammation in people with SCI to reduce NP. Participants will complete a 12-week exercise trial consisting of 20 to 30-minutes of moderate to vigorous physical activity 3 times a week in accordance with SCI specific exercise guidelines. Blood samples will be taken to monitor the levels of inflammation in the blood and NP will be assessed using a validated subjective measure. This study will allow us to better understand how exercise can reduce NP in people with SCI and more specifically what role exercise plays in inflammation. This will allow clinicians, rehabilitation specialists, and other healthcare professionals to create better non-pharmaceutical interventions aimed to reduce inflammation and NP in people with SCI.

Malgre la prevalence croissante de cette maladie complexe liee a l'obesite, l'age et l'historique familial, les therapies sont soit risquees ou ont un faible taux de succes. column36: Navigating Sexuality and Sexual Health Among Cis and Trans Youth and Young Women Living with HIV in a Criminalized Context
column37: Young people, especially young women, face disproportionate barriers to health and social services access. The late teens and early twenties present a critical moment of development, where cis and trans youth and young women living with HIV (YWLWH) face new challenges as their sexual development coincides with greater agency and autonomy over their biomedical disease management. Negotiations of sexual relationships can be complicated for all young people, but the added complexities of living with HIV, including the criminalization of HIV non-disclosure, stigmatization, as well as the impact of the social and structural vulnerabilities that affect many YWLWH, further exacerbates this dialog. For YWLWH since birth, and for those who have acquired HIV in their young adult life, there is a need for innovative programmatic and health care provision strategies that are informed by these distinct experiences, and the unique stigma that influences their sexual and social development. This study will use participatory and community based research methods, to inform community-led and evidence-based HIV/AIDS policy and programing for, with and by YWLWH.

column36: Targeting the Genital Microbiota to Reduce Human Immunodeficiency Virus Transmission Among African, Caribbean, and other Black Women
column37: African, Caribbean, and other Black (ACB) women experience disproportionately high HIV risk in Ontario. A significant portion of this risk may be due to variation in the types of bacteria in the female genital tract (FGT), collectively known as the vaginal microbiome. The types of bacteria that colonize the vagina differ between women, and the vaginal microbiome composition has been linked to reproductive health outcomes including HIV acquisition after a sexual exposure. High diversity of bacterial species in the vaginal microbiome may lead to a condition known as bacterial vaginosis (BV). Although BV is often asymptomatic, it has been linked to increased HIV susceptibility, and unfortunately is more common in ACB women. Antibiotic treatment of BV can reverse these changes in the short term, but BV usually recurs within a few months. In addition, my supervisor's research group has found that antibiotic treatment actually increased some immune indicators of HIV risk. The proposed research aims to test novel microbiome-focused clinical strategies, both antibiotic- and probiotic-based, to reduce HIV susceptibility among ACB women. I hypothesize that standard antibiotic treatment for BV will increase certain immune indicators of HIV susceptibility and recruit HIV target cells to the vaginal lining, but that addition of a novel probiotic will restore the vaginal microbiome to a state that is protective against HIV. The elevated HIV risk faced by ACB women emphasizes the urgent need for better clinical strategies to reduce HIV susceptibility among this population. We hope that the results of this proposed research can inform future clinical strategies to reduce HIV susceptibility among women and the ACB community.

column36: Studying the metabolic pathways of cholesterol from different lipoprotein sources in hepatocytes
column37: Atherosclerosis is a chronic progressive disease accounting for most cardiovascular disease cases. It is caused by the accumulation of lipoproteins in the arteries. Components of these lipoproteins, such as cholesterol and protein, form plaques which harden and narrow the arteries. This accumulation can block blood flow. The liver regulates the levels of these atherogenic lipoproteins by altering their release from the liver and their removal from the blood. Liver cells, called hepatocytes, are capable of removing lipoproteins from the bloodstream and then releasing them within the cell. The lipoprotein is then degraded, and its cholesterol is released in the hepatocyte. In theory, the degraded lipoprotein governs intracellular levels of cholesterol. Our work suggests that the outcome of cholesterol regulation depends on the lipoprotein and the cell studied. In hepatocytes, most of the cholesterol from low-density lipoproteins (LDL) is released into the bloodstream within atherogenic lipoproteins. By contrast, chylomicron remnants (CR) regulate cholesterol levels within the hepatocyte. I hypothesize that in the hepatocyte, LDL cholesterol and CR cholesterol are delivered to distinct compartments to carry out different functions. To test this hypothesis, I will observe hepatocytes under a microscope and map the itinerary of LDL and CR cholesterol. In addition, I will identify the tools hepatocytes use to distinguish LDLs from CRs, and the components that process these lipoproteins. Our goal is to characterize lipoprotein metabolism within liver cells to better understand the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis. This project also has the potential to identify drug targets to reduce the levels of atherogenic lipoproteins released, thus broadening the therapeutic window.

column37: Compte tenu de l'avancement en age de la population, les previsions concernant la prevalence de maladies cognitives telles que la maladie d'Alzheimer sont a la hausse (Societe Alzheimer du Canada, 2016). Dans le but d'attenuer les symptomes ainsi que d'ameliorer la qualite de vie des patients atteints, de plus en plus de recherches se sont penches sur les bienfaits de la therapie musicale. Malgre un interet grandissant pour ce sujet, peu de recherches systematiques ont examine ses effets sur les symptomes depressifs vecus par les gens souffrant de cette maladie. Ce projet a donc pour objectif de contribuer a l'avancement des connaissances en mesurant les effets d'une intervention d'ecoute musicale personnalisee et realisee a domicile sur les symptomes depressifs de la maladie d'Alzheimer en debut d'evolution. 60 participants seront separes en deux groupes independants. Le premier groupe (controle) ecoutera des sons tires de l'environnement alors que le deuxieme groupe (experimental) sera expose a l'intervention musicale. Le tout se deroulera sur une periode de 6 semaines et chaque session sera d'une duree de 20 minutes. Il est prevu que l'ecoute musicale diminuera la presence de symptomes depressifs au cours des sessions et que ses effets seront plus significatifs que ceux de l'ecoute de sons dans l'environnement. L'intervention musicale a l'avantage d'etre non-invasive, peu couteuse et facile a integrer dans la vie des patients. Elle est une donc solution pratique pour les gens vivant encore a domicile et ses effets ont le potentiel d'etre benefiques en debut de maladie.

column36: Sex differences and gut microbiota-based treatments for stroke repair
column37: Stroke is a devastating disease that affects 50,000 Canadians every year. Unfortunately, there are few effective treatments for stroke, highlighting the need for new therapies. The recent discovery that bacteria in the gut can affect the outcome of many neurological conditions has generated significant interest in targeting gut bacteria and their by-products as a potential therapeutic approach. Indeed, in the context of stroke, there is a significant change in the diversity of bacteria found in the gut that is associated with functional impairment seen after injury. Interestingly, sex differences in gut bacteria are apparent in human populations. It is also well established that males and females show different outcomes following stroke. Considering that sex differences are observed in gut microbiota and stroke prognosis, the goal of this project is to identify whether there is differential regulation of gut bacteria after stroke in males and females and if this differentially impacts stroke outcomes in males and females. To address this, we will use transplant paradigms in mice to determine how male gut bacteria influence female stroke outcomes, and vice versa. Importantly, we will also examine whether treatment with bacterial by-products that have been shown to improve functional outcomes in animal models of neurological disease, differentially affect stroke outcomes in males and females. This research will be the first to examine sex differences in gut bacteria after stroke and how this impacts stroke outcomes, and will be key to establishing novel, gut-based therapeutic interventions in the future.

column36: The Design and Validation of Clinical Decision-Support Algorithm for Clinicians to Help in the Prescribing of Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone Blockers for Diabetic Nephroprotection in Older Patients
column37: Chronic kidney disease is a serious condition where the kidneys' function progressively declines, which may ultimately result in a need for kidney replacement therapy such as dialysis. After age, diabetes is the most important risk factor for developing kidney disease, as 40% of kidney disease cases were due to diabetes. Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone blockers (RAAB) is a class of medications that have protective effects from kidney disease in patients with diabetes. Although there is an evidence on the importance of prescribing RAAB in patients with diabetes, 57% of older patients are not receiving RAAB in fear of their side effects, or underestimation of their beneficial effects in frail older patients. That would result in increased cases of older patients who end up in dialysis units and who suffer painful and costly complications. Clinicians need to incorporate knowledge from clinical trials and balance it with their patients' unique factors (such as patients' level of independence and remaining life expectancy) to help decide when to prescribe RAAB for their older patients. This project aims at developing and validating a tool to aid clinicians when prescribing RAAB to older patients with diabetes. While being based on the latest medical evidence, this tool will consider the patients' level of independence and remaining life expectancy when deciding to stop, resume or start RAAB for kidney protection. We propose to conduct a thorough literature review to design the tool and will validate its accuracy and clearness through consulting a panel of experts. The use of this tool in the daily clinical practice will ensure that older patients with diabetes will receive RAAB when eligible, and will be protected from complications of kidney disease, and dialysis eventually.

column36: Characterization of Molecular Partners of the Programmed Cell Death Protein 1/Programmed Death-ligand 1 Immune Checkpoint in Tumour Cells
column37: Immune checkpoints are vital regulators of the host immune system. They provide a balance between co-stimulators and inhibitors of immune cells, preventing over-stimulation that can otherwise lead to inflammation and auto-immunity. However, tumour cells can take advantage of this innate system as a way to deactivate immune cells and evade the host immune system, termed immune escape. Programmed Death 1 (PD-1) is one such immune checkpoint found on immune cells. It interacts with Programmed Death-Ligand 1 (PD-L1) on tumour cells and results in the deactivation of immune cells, conferring immune escape. Strategies have been developed to interfere with this PD-1/PD-L1 interaction, including drugs called immune checkpoint blockers. These immune checkpoint blockers have demonstrated exceptionally high response rates in patients with advanced stages of cancer, providing new promise. However, there are limitations to the current use of immune checkpoint blockers. For reasons not yet known, the majority of patients do not significantly benefit from this therapy, despite the high response rates. This demonstrates that there is still a lot to be known about the PD-1/PD-L1 axis. Quite recent research has elucidated that the PD-1/PD-L1 interaction not only affects immune cells, but also exerts a change on the tumour cells, causing them to exhibit a more malignant phenotype, including drug resistance and metastasis. Our proposed research aims to identify proteins within the tumour cells interacting with PD-L1 that facilitate malignant progression. This knowledge would provide us greater insight into the underpinnings of immune checkpoints, and could ultimately impact the timing of therapies as well as potentially elucidate new druggable targets.

column36: Target validation of ACLY as a novel anti-cancer drug target for hepatocellular carcinoma
column37: ATP citrate lyase (ACLY) performs an essential role in de novo lipogenesis by catalyzing the synthesis of cytosolic acetyl-CoA. De novo lipogenesis is upregulated in cancer in order to compensate for the metabolic demands of rapid cell proliferation. This is because lipid is an important macromolecule for cell proliferation due to its roles in membrane biogenesis, cell signaling and energy production/storage. Therefore, it is not surprising that ACLY is upregulated in various types of cancer and correlates with poor patient prognosis. However, the role of ACLY in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains largely unknown. Currently, the net 5 year survival rate of HCC is 19% and its incidence is rapidly increasing in Canada. Unfortunately, Sorafenib and Lenvatinib, the lone first-line standard of treatment drugs for HCC, could only extend median survival by 3 - 4 months. Thus, validation of ACLY as a novel drug target for HCC either alone or in combination with these drugs is of critical interest for improving the standard of care for HCC. The proposed study aims to discover and validate the role of ACLY in HCC through both pharmacological and genetic inhibition of ACLY activity.

column36: Utilite clinique des tests d'oscillometrie respiratoire en ajout a l'evaluation clinique de l'asthme chez les enfants d'age prescolaire
column37: L'asthme est une maladie respiratoire comportant deux sous-types caracterises par des symptomes persistants ou recurrents. Le principal test utilise pour diagnostiquer le sous-type d'asthme est appele spirometrie, ce qui necessite que les patients expirent avec force. Il est difficile d'identifier le sous-type d'asthme chez les enfants de moins de 6 ans, car la spirometrie n'est pas adaptee aux enfants de ce groupe d'age. De plus, il est difficile de se procurer des appareils de spirometrie dans la communaute, ou 85% des enfants asthmatiques sont traites. Une alternative interessante est un test appele l'oscillometrie (OS), qui exige que les enfants respirent normalement, un test plus adapte aux enfants de moins de 6 ans. A date, l'utilite de ce test pour suivre et ajuster le traitement d'enfants asthmatiques n'a pas ete formellement etudiee. Cette etude va evaluer l'utilite de l'OS pour identifier le sous-type d'asthme chez les enfants de moins de 6, ainsi que l'effet des tests reguliers d'OS sur les medicaments prescrits par les medecins pour controler les symptomes asthmatiques de leurs patients. Pour ce faire, les donnees de deux grandes bases de donnees fournie par les cliniques d'asthme de deux hopitaux pediatriques a Montreal seront utilisees. L'etude comparera les donnees d'enfants asthmatiques ages de moins de 6 ans appartenant a deux groupes distinct. Un groupe est constitue de 390 enfants qui ont subi des tests reguliers par OS, tandis que l'autre groupe est constitue de 811 enfants qui n'ont jamais subi de tests d'OS. Si les tests d'OS s'averent utiles, la commercialisation recente d'appareils d'OS portables ne necessitant aucun professionnel pour les operer, permettra aux medecins de la communaute de beneficier de l'utilisation de cette technique.

column36: Role of Eosinophils During Bacterial Infection
column37: Eosinophils are a type of immune cell that are present in the intestinal tract of healthy individuals. During inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) the number of intestinal eosinophils rises, and a higher number of eosinophils is associated with more severe disease. In addition, IBD leaves patients at higher risk of infection with harmful bacteria. The role of eosinophils in this context is unknown: are eosinophils helpful in contributing to a protective immune response against bacteria or is the presence of eosinophils allowing the bacteria to thrive in the intestinal tract? This research project aims to determine whether, and how, the presence of eosinophils alters the outcome of infection with a bacterial pathogen. I hypothesize that eosinophils promote intestinal colonization by bacterial pathogens. To test this hypothesis, I will orally infect wild-type and eosinophil-deficient mice with a model bacterial pathogen and track the resulting inflammation, pathology and bacterial burdens along the intestinal tract. The use of these mouse models will allow for the determination of causal relationships between eosinophils and susceptibility to bacterial pathogens. The Reynolds lab has state of the art research equipment in addition to all other necessary resources for the completion of this project. Canada has one of the highest rates of inflammatory bowel disease worldwide. To better treat and manage IBD it is necessary to understand how immune cell types such as eosinophils contribute to disease. As well as contributing to health knowledge, carrying out this research will allow me to acquire the necessary skills and techniques to continue into doctoral studies and ultimately establish a career as a leader in immunology research.

column36: Trajectory of brain and cognitive development of children with CHD: neuropsychology and functional connectivity
column37: Congenital heart diseases are cardiac malformations that occur during the intrauterine period and are amongst the most common in infants. It is estimated that 8.23 out of 1000 babies are born with a congenital heart disease. Depending on the malformations' severity, some of the babies have to undergo one or many restorative surgeries in the days following their birth. About 50% of the survivors develop impairments in one or many areas of their functioning (learning skills, speech and language, motor skills, social skills, memory, attention, and executive functions). Several impacts on the quality of life of these children are due to these neurodevelopmental delays, including significant academic, social and behavioral difficulties. My project aims to document the development of brain networks in children with congenital heart diseases. More specifically, I want to compare brain networks of children with congenital heart diseases to those of healthy children at 42 months old and investigate the relationship between brain networks and developmental profiles. In an exploratory way, I will also document the developmental trajectory of the brain networks in children with congenital heart disease, between 4 and 42 months of age. To do so, children with congenital heart disease and healthy children will undergo a developmental evaluation using behavioral tests. We will also measure their functional brain connectivity using near infrared spectroscopy (NIRS). A better comprehension of brain development and its relationship with developmental outcomes will allow a better understanding of the neural substrates of cognitive and motor disabilities in CHD. As a long term goal, this will help to provide more adapted intervention strategies to this pediatric population.

column36: Resurrecting ancestral receptors to uncover the origins of drug specificity
column37: As healthcare improves, the world's population is aging, and the number of people with age-related cognitive impairment is on the rise. This is creating economic and social burdens on society. Few options exist for treating cognitive impairment, however existing strategies emphasize the importance of cholinergic signaling. Pharmaceutical companies have begun to target acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) on cholinergic neurons as a way to modulate synaptic activity. The most abundant AChR in the brain is the alpha7 AChR. Positive allosteric modulators (PAMs) of alpha7 have been developed to strengthen synaptic response, however little is known about the location of their binding sites, or the residues that mediate their action. We hypothesize that different alpha7 PAMs act through divergent sites in the transmembrane domain. Unlike the acetylcholine binding site, PAM sites are under less evolutionary pressure, and thus tend to be more diverse within homologous proteins. For instance, PNU-120596 (PNU) potentiates mammalian alpha7 AChRs, but has no effect on the C. elegans alpha7 homolog, ACR-16. Using an evolutionary biochemistry approach, this project will replay the evolutionary trajectory of alpha7 in the lab. By resurrecting ancestral alpha7 subunits and testing them in the lab, we will identify evolutionary intervals where sensitivity to a particular PAM arose. We will then identify the amino acids responsible for PAM sensitivity, and the number of PAM molecules required for potentiation. Once complete, this project will deepen our understanding of how PAMs interact with alpha7, and will offer new insight into drug specificity. Ultimately, these results will aid the rational design of small-molecules for treating cognitive diseases through targeting of alpha7 AChRs.

column36: Patient reported dose adequacy in injectable opioid agonist treatment: the role of patient involvement in dose decision-making
column37: Opioid use disorder (OUD) is a chronic condition where people sometimes continue using opioids despite negative consequences and potential risks, other times they might: engage into treatment, temporarily or permanently stop use (without treatment), or relapse into drug use. For people struggling with an OUD, the most effective care option is opioid agonist treatment (OAT). OAT usually involves prescribing an oral medication (e.g. methadone, buprenorphine, slow-release morphine) that blocks the physical need to use street opioids. Some patients still inject opioids even if OAT is available and will respond better to injectable opioid agonist treatment (iOAT), therefore reducing the harms, risks, and costs associated with criminalized and untreated street opioid (e.g. illicit heroin, fentanyl) use, such as fatal overdose. Research into oral OAT indicates that involving patients in dose decision-making improves the likelihood that each patient receives an adequate dose: a dose which is individualized, more effective at retaining the patient, and has a better chance of helping the patient reduce their use of street opioids. Dose adequacy is measured through a clinical questionnaire which asks the patient about their OUD symptoms (e.g. withdrawals, street opioid use) and their experience of the OAT dose (e.g. overmedication symptoms, reduced cravings). Since dose adequacy is associated with better outcomes in oral OAT, I will study dose adequacy in patients new to iOAT (about 350 patients). Furthermore, since involving the patient in dose decision-making plays the biggest role in improving dose adequacy (in oral OAT), I will measure this factor and examine its relationship with dose-adequacy in iOAT. This research will help inform and support effective provision of iOAT.

column36: Novel Strategies for the Restoration of Vision Loss in Age-Related Macular Degeneration
column37: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a disease that results in the deterioration of tissue in the macula, the central portion of the eye. The macula contains photoreceptor cells which play a key role in transforming light into signals that our brain can process, enabling us to perceive vision. Progressive loss of these cells due to AMD ultimately leads to blindness. In North America alone, AMD is the leading cause of irreversible vision loss in individuals over the age of 60. While current AMD therapies focus on slowing disease progression, they are not able to reverse blindness. Thus, the overall goal of my project is to restore vision in patients who have lost their sight due to AMD. One potential strategy to restore vision is the replacement of lost photoreceptors through regeneration. In cold-blooded animals such as fish, regeneration is in fact a common injury response. For this process to occur, cells known as Muller glia (MG) activate sets of genes that trigger reprogramming of the cell. This allows MG to rapidly divide and generate various specialized cells, ultimately replacing the damaged tissue. Although MG are found in mammals, they are unable to enter the regenerative process. I suspect that this is due to a failure of mammalian MG to switch on the same genes that are activated in fish. I propose that the introduction of these genes into mammalian MG will trigger regeneration. Using a mouse model of AMD, I will introduce these genes in conjunction with genes that specifically reprogram mammalian MG into photoreceptors. I intend to identify a combination of genes that stimulate mammalian regeneration of functional macular tissue. Ultimately, these genes can be used in a novel therapeutic drug that will restore vision in patients suffering from AMD.

column36: Role des macrophages senescents dans les maladies associees a l'age.
column37: La senescence est un arret permanent de la division cellulaire agissant comme mecanisme anti-tumoral. Les cellules senescentes produisent beaucoup de secretions, appelees <<senescent-associated secretory phenotype>> (SASP). Le SASP comprend beaucoup de secretions solubles (appelees cytokines) pro-inflammatoires. Ainsi, a court terme, le SASP contribue a activer le systeme immunitaire pour eliminer les cellules senescentes, ce qui est benefique. Par contre, a long terme, le SASP provoque une inflammation chronique et une dysfonction tissulaire. Il a ete montre que, dans les modeles de souris, les cellules senescentes s'accumulent avec l'age et que leur elimination pouvait ameliorer la sante des souris vieillissantes et meme diminuer la presentation de maladies associees au vieillissement. Aussi, il a ete montre que les macrophages representent une large portion des cellules senescentes. Ces macrophages senescents ont une forte activite pro-cancer et sont entre autres impliques dans l'atherosclerose. Par ailleurs, les cellules senescentes secretent plus de vesicules extracellulaires (VE) que les cellules non-senescentes, suggerant les que VE sont importantes dans le SASP. Nous voulons donc developper un modele in vitro de macrophages senescents et caracteriser leurs secretions solubles (cytokines) et vesiculaires (VE). De plus, nous voulons etudier l'effet de ces secretions sur d'autres cellules. A plus long terme, ces etudes fourniront des informations essentielles pour mieux eliminer les macrophages senescents, qui ont un fort impact sur le vieillissement et ses maladies reliees, ou a tout le moins pour diminuer l'impact de leurs secretions sur les cellules environnantes et sur l'organisme.

column36: Single-cell analysis to identify the cellular origins of pediatric brain tumors
column37: Pediatric brain tumors (PBT) are the leading cause of cancer-related death and the second most common diagnosed malignancy in children in Canada. Despite aggressive therapy, for many tumor types, outcomes have not changed in the last three decades. Survival is very low, and patients that do survive are left with severe lifelong side-effects. For many tumor types, the initial event that causes a brain tumor occurs during normal development. During development, cells undergo a sequence of coordinated changes in gene expression that has to be finely controlled, and alterations in this process often cause disease. Our goal is to identify the precise timing of these initial disease-causing events for several tumor types of uncertain origin. For this, we propose to assemble a large collection of datasets at the single-cell resolution for both tumor samples and normal developing tissues. We will develop the computational tools to analyze and integrate these large datasets. Finally, we will employ these novel strategies to characterize additional samples from patient cohorts. This project aims to address a critical gap in research on pediatric brain tumors. Establishment of experimental models for specific tumor types and improving therapeutic strategies are both challenging because for many PBT, the origins of the tumor are unknown. By generating large-scale datasets measuring gene expression in both tumors and developing tissues, we will provide a comprehensive map of gene expression changes that may be altered in childhood brain tumors, which can provide therapeutic targets. This has the potential for major impact on the treatment of these cancers.

column36: Effects of testosterone replacement therapy on physiological and behavioural parameters among hypogonadal men with type 2 diabetes
column37: The Canadian Diabetes Association estimates that 30% of the adult population in Ontario will have prediabetes or diabetes by 2020. Prospective studies indicate that low testosterone (T) is a significant risk factor for the development of type 2 diabetes (T2D). Further, upwards of 40% of men with T2D meet clinical criteria for hypogonadism. Recent work indicates that testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) in hypogonadal T2D men has many beneficial effects, including decreasing insulin resistance, inflammation, fat mass, and increasing sexual function. Despite many of its positive effects, no studies have investigated the behavioural consequences of TRT among men with T2D. This is particularly problematic in light of basic endocrinology research indicating that T can modulate important behavioural outcomes including aggression, risk-taking, and economic decision-making. The current proposal will systematically assess, for the first time, the effects of TRT on physiological and behaviour processes in hypogonadal men with T2D, enabling health care practitioners and patients to make more fully informed decisions - in consideration of both the health and social benefits/costs - about whether TRT is a good treatment option for T2D.

column36: Les facteurs psychosociaux influencant la pratique d'activite physique chez des survivantes du cancer du sein
column37: La survivance au cancer du sein est consideree comme une maladie chronique necessitant l'adoption de saines habitudes de vie afin de prevenir l'exacerbation des symptomes residuels, la diminution potentielle de la qualite de vie ou alors, la recidive du cancer. Neanmoins, ceci constitue un defi pour les survivantes, car la plupart vivent des difficultes biopsychosociales telle que la fatigue persistante qui constitue une consequence majeure des traitements. Ainsi, la majorite des survivantes ne rencontrent pas les lignes directrices en matiere de pratique reguliere d'activites physiques moderees. Considerant que les infirmieres ont un role a jouer dans la promotion des saines habitudes de vie, que la sedentarite des survivantes est un enjeu de sante pour les personnes touchees et un enjeu de sante publique, il s'avere donc pertinent de mieux connaitre les relations entre les variables psychosociales et l'intention de pratiquer des activites physiques moderees chez des survivantes du cancer du sein. column36: Stimulator of Interferon Genes Pathway Activation as an Immunotherapeutic Strategy for Soft Tissue Sarcoma
column37: Sarcomas are aggressive cancers derived from bone, muscle, fat, and other connective tissue. Sarcomas are relatively rare; thus, grossly understudied. Conventional treatment consists of radiation, surgery, and chemotherapy, and is rigorous, toxic, and may result in life-long post-operative disabilities from amputations. Furthermore, this treatment is ineffective as roughly 20% of patients develop metastases. Clearly, further research into safer, more effective strategies are needed. Recently, immune-based therapies have shown promise in regard to several cancers, including lung cancer and melanoma, and several immunotherapy drugs are in clinical trials. Immunotherapy provides a safer alternative treatment to systemic cytotoxic chemotherapy. One immunotherapy in particular caught our interest: stimulator of interferon genes (STING) activation by 5,6-dimethylxanthenone-4-acetic acid (DMXAA) administration. DMXAA is a potent activator of mouse STING. Previous studies found that STING activation is very effective in treating some types of cancers as it upregulates type 1 interferons, which aid in the regulation and development of immune responses. However, STING activation as a therapeutic approach has not been studied in sarcomas. Herein, we aim to study STING activation as an immunotherapeutic strategy to treat one of the most common adult sarcomas, undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (UPS). Our research plan is to use a mouse model of UPS to test the therapeutic potential of DMXAA. We will monitor the growth or rejection of tumours following DMXAA treatment and uncover the underlying mechanisms of intra-tumoural STING activation. This project is clinically compelling and employs an innovative, safer approach to sarcoma treatment.

column36: Emotional Contagion as a Risk Factor in Inpatient Eating Disorder Treatment Programs
column37: There has been mixed feedback regarding the efficacy of inpatient treatment programs for anorexia nervosa, with patients responding positively to peer support, but also reporting body weight comparison and competition (Colton & Pistrang, 2004). There is thus some concern regarding social contagion within inpatient eating disorder (ED) treatment groups, as a subculture of further disordered eating habits can develop among peers (Vandereycken, 2011). There is a need to examine risk factors in EDinpatient programs. Dispositional emotional contagion could be a measure of risk for social contagion among inpatients, as it measures one's propensity to mimic the emotion of others (Hatfield, Rapson, Le, Decety, & Ickes, 2009). This study hypothesizes that higher dispositional emotional contagion will be correlated with poorer treatment outcomesin ED patients in inpatient programs, but not in outpatient programs. There will two groups recruited for this study. One group of participants will be from an inpatient program, and the second group will be from an outpatient program. Participants must score 20 or higher on the Eating Attitudes Test (EAT-26) to qualify (Garner, Olmsted, Bohr & Garfinkel, 1982). Participants will also complete the Emotional Contagion Scale (ECS), and will be paired across groups based on similar ECS scores (Doherty, 1997). Each week for a period of two months, participants will be issued the EAT-26. The results will be analyzed to determine if there is a statistically significant difference between the change in EAT scores for those in inpatient and outpatient groups, mediated by ECS scores. This study has the potential to better inform individual needs in ED treatment programs within the field of Clinical Psychology.

column37: Gonorrhea is a common sexually transmitted infection, caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Prevalence of the infection is rising, and many strains of the pathogen are developing resistance to antibiotics. N. gonorrhoeae infects the mucosal surfaces of the genital tract and nasal pharynx of humans. However, mucosal barriers are never sterile; instead, they are naturally inhabited by a community of non-pathogenic microorganisms, collectively called the microbiota. N. gonorrhoeae must therefore compete with the microbiota during its infection. The purpose of my project is to elucidate the interactions between the genital tract microbiota and N. gonorrhoeae infection. I will use humanized mouse models to study this system, and I will test and compare different strains of N. gonorrhoeae, since different strains of the pathogen can have different characteristics. Over the course of N. gonorrhoeae infection, the genital tracts of the mice will be washed out to collect genetic material from the microbiota. Using high-throughput sequencing techniques, the diversity and relative abundances of the microbiota can be assessed, as can the progress and intensity of the N. gonorrhoeae infection. By examining how the diversity of the genital tract microbiota changes over the course of infection, I can determine if N. gonorrhoeae alters the microbiota to create a more favorable environment for itself. Furthermore, by comparing the responses of mice with a healthy microbiota and those with a depleted one, I will be able to investigate whether the genital tract microbiota confer a protective effect against N. gonorrhoeae infection to the host. This will be the first study to fully characterize the role of the genital tract microbiota in the pathogenesis of N. gonorrhoeae.

column36: Genomic Regulation of Pediatric Age Acceleration: Relevance for Child Mental Health
column37: Epigenetic clocks have been validated as clinically relevant biomarkers with the ability to predict adverse health effects in adults. These clocks use genome methylation information at specific sites in the genome to calculate the epigenetic (biological) age of an individual. Epigenetic age acceleration, which is the difference between an individual's chronological age and biological age, predicts many negative outcomes including psychopathology in adults. Recently, an epigenetic clock specific to children - the pediatric clock - has been developed and shown to be of relevance to child neurodevelopment. Our research group is investigating the effects of environmental and biological influences on pediatric age acceleration and its implications on child development and mental health outcomes. We have found that the early care environment predicts variation in pediatric age acceleration. We aim to identify and assess the functionality of genetic biomarkers associated with epigenetic aging, and to determine how epigenetic age acceleration associates with later child psychopathology. A meta-analysis using 5 cohorts (N=1229) will be used for a genome wide association analysis of pediatric age acceleration and for investigation into psychopathologies using parent report symptom checklists available for all children in these cohorts. Analysis of the pediatric clock and its implications provides a unique opportunity to observe genetic and environmental impacts at the level of the individual. This is a necessary step in the direction of personalized medicine in child and youth mental health.

column36: The role of zDHHC9-mediated protein palmitoylation in activity-induced synaptic strengthening
column37: Intellectual disability (ID) is characterized by limitations in cognitive abilities including learning, reasoning and problem solving. While it is known that ID has a strong hereditary component and is caused by disruptions in proper brain development, our understanding of the genes associated with ID and how disrupting their function leads to pathology is still in its infancy. 'Palmitoylation' is a biochemical process involving the reversible addition of palmitate to proteins. Proper palmitoylation of proteins has been shown to be important for the differentiation and outgrowth of nerve cells (neurons), as well as the development and plasticity of specialized connections between neurons, called 'synapses'. Loss-of-function mutations in one of the enzymes that mediate palmitoylation, zDHHC9, has been identified in 2% of all patients with X-linked intellectual disability (XLID). A high proportion of these patients also exhibit epileptic seizures. Our lab has previously demonstrated that zDHHC9 is exceedingly important for the formation of inhibitory synapses and the plasticity of synaptic connections. My goal is to further our understanding of the role of zDHHC9 by determining all downstream substrates for zDHHC9 as well as determining which substrates are specifically palmitoylated by zDHHC9 following a learning event or increased synaptic activity. Together, we propose that identifying the molecular mechanisms that underlie zDHHC9 function in synapse formation and activity-mediated synaptic plasticity is important in order to understand the changes that lead to disease and for advancement of targeted therapeutic interventions.

column36: Effets des contraceptifs oraux sur l'extinction de la peur : Implications pour le developpement du cerveau
column37: Des la puberte, deux fois plus de femmes que d'hommes souffrent d'un trouble anxieux ou d'un trouble de stress post-traumatique. Ces troubles se caracterisent par des niveaux de peur accrus et une capacite amoindrie a reguler la peur. Des pistes ont suggere que les hormones sexuelles, particulierement l'estrogene, pourraient expliquer cette difference entre les sexes. Accedant au cerveau, ces hormones ont un impact sur les structures liees a la regulation de la peur. Des etudes ont demontre que la regulation de la peur etait defaillante chez les femmes ayant des faibles niveaux d'estrogene et celles prenant des contraceptifs oraux (abolissant les variations du cycle menstruel en maintenant une faible secretion de ces hormones). Or, aucune etude n'a considere le moment de la prise de contraceptifs oraux et leurs effets potentiellement durables. A l'adolescence, puisque 1) la prise de contraceptifs oraux est frequemment initiee, 2) le cerveau n'est pas dument developpe et 3) les hormones sexuelles sont particulierement presentes a ce moment, il est pertinent d'examiner si la prise de contraceptifs oraux pendant le developpement cerebral peut modifier la regulation de la peur a long terme. A l'aide d'un modele de laboratoire valide, nous examinerons les patrons d'apprentissage de la peur et la regulation de celle-ci chez des femmes ayant utilise des contraceptifs oraux a l'adolescence, comparativement a celles en ayant utilise a l'age adulte, celles n'en ayant jamais utilise et aux hommes. Sachant que des millions de femmes utilisent ces contraceptifs, ce projet favorisera la reflexion quant aux lignes directrices en matiere de contraception et pourra soutenir l'importance de creer des methodes d'intervention individualisees chez les femmes souffrant de troubles anxieux.

column36: Genetic Associations with Aortic Stenosis in Non-European Populations
column37: Aortic Stenosis (AS) is a common form of valve disease that leads to heart failure and death. Despite its high prevalence in North America, the only current treatment option for AS is surgery. In recent years, genome-wide association studies have been used to help understand the genetic causes of AS. However, these studies have been restricted exclusively to populations of European ancestry. Without robust replication of findings in non-Europeans, results from these studies will not be broadly applicable. In addition, pathways unique to other ethnicities will remain undiscovered. To close this gap, I propose to conduct genome-wide association studies for AS in Black and Hispanic populations. I will first assess whether genetic variants shown to contribute to AS in European populations have the same effect in these ethnicities. I will then look for novel variants that are specific to Black and Hispanic populations. To further understand my results, I will determine if genetic ancestry helps to explain racial differences in the prevalence of AS. The results from my project will help to extend the benefits of AS research to under-represented populations.

column36: La cigarette electronique est-elle une alternative << sante >> a la cigarette combustible conventionnelle? La reponse cardiorespiratoire, vasculaire, immunitaire et thrombotique sous des conditions de stress physique et psychologique.
column37: La consommation de cigarettes combustibles est un risque majeur pour le developpement des maladies cardiovasculaires et des maladies pulmonaires. Recemment, l'utilisation de la cigarette electronique (e-cigarette) s'est presentee comme une alternative a la consommation de cigarettes combustibles. Le peu d'etudes actuelles sur la e-cigarette laisse croire a son innocuite et meme a sa potentielle efficacite pour aider a la cessation de la consommation de cigarettes combustibles. Cependant, la nicotine contenue dans la e-cigarette est un puissant addictif pouvant presager une utilisation prolongee du produit. Ainsi, il est necessaire de s'interroger quant aux effets possibles sur la sante (risques ou benefices) de l'usage des e-cigarettes en tant qu'alternative a la cigarette combustible. Les jeunes adultes sont particulierement concernes par les effets du tabagisme en raison du taux eleve de consommation de produits du tabac de cette population (31%). Les effets deleteres de la consommation de tabac sont deja observables chez cette tranche de la population lors de la pratique d'exercice physique ou de l'exposition a un stress psychologique. Les stress physiques et psychologiques induisent des anomalies similaires des processus cardiovasculaires, respiratoires et inflammatoires menant a un risque accru pour le developpement de maladies chroniques. Cependant, aucune etude n'a demontre l'influence de l'utilisation de la e-cigarette sur les reponses physiologiques sous diverses conditions de stress. Une meilleure connaissance des effets de la consommation de e-cigarette aura un impact significatif sur la sante des populations en orientant les decisions des legislateurs, des professionnels de la sante et des patients quant a la consommation et a l'encadrement de ce produit.

column36: Characterizing and exploiting novel role of BRCA1 in ribosomal DNA control
column37: Increased risk of breast and ovarian cancer is associated with mutations in the breast cancer protein (BRCA1), which is one of the proteins that protects the genome from damage. BRCA1 has been shown to prevent the accumulation of potentially DNA damaging structures, known as R-loops. My first objective is to study whether BRCA1 protects the genome from damage by preventing R-loop accumulation at the DNA region that encodes protein synthesizing machineries, known as ribosomes. To study this, I will use breast cancer cells that have the normal BRCA1 and examine the level of R-loops in presence and absence of BRCA1. To assess if the genome is being protected from damage, I will examine the level of DNA damage, problems with DNA replication, and defects in ribosome synthesis. My second objective is to study whether increasing R-loop accumulation at ribosomal DNA (rDNA) in BRCA1-mutated breast cancer cells will increase DNA damage, stop cell growth and increase cell death. I will increase R-loop accumulation in the cells by getting rid of two proteins that prevent R-loop accumulation, and I will examine if the cells exhibit increased R-loop levels, DNA damage, disrupted ribosome synthesis, increased problems with DNA replication, and increased cell death. My work may point to novel therapeutic strategies that exploit the partly elevated R-loop levels of BRCA1-deficient cancer cells to further exacerbate R-loop accumulation and selectively kill cancer cells.

column36: Identification precoce de la maladie d'Alzheimer: une etude longitudinale de la cohorte CIMA-Q
column37: Le diagnostic de la maladie d'Alzheimer est etabli lorsque les criteres de demence sont remplis, stade auquel les dommages structurels au cerveau sont importants, nuisant a l'efficacite des interventions. Plusieurs etudes se sont donc interessees aux stades qui precederaient la demence, le declin cognitif subjectif et le trouble cognitif leger, pour tenter d'identifier des signes precoces de la maladie. Un des signes se trouverait au niveau de l'activation cerebrale. Les personnes avec une demence montreraient des niveaux d'activations cerebrales plus bas que les personnes agees sans probleme cognitif (hypoactivations), alors que celles avec un trouble cognitif leger montreraient des niveaux plus eleves (hyperactivations). Toutefois, on ne sait pas si ces hyperactivations sont presentes chez les personnes avec un declin cognitif subjectif, et aucune etude n'a examine l'evolution des hyperactivations dans la progression de la maladie. La presente etude comparera l'activite cerebrale a deux ans d'intervalle chez des personnes avec un declin cognitif subjectif et un trouble cognitif leger du Consortium pour l'identification precoce de la maladie d'Alzheimer - Quebec (CIMA-Q). Nous tenterons d'evaluer de quelle facon les hyperactivations cerebrales prediraient la progression des symptomes. L'imagerie par resonance magnetique fonctionnelle (IRMf) sera utilisee lors d'une tache de memoire. Examiner les activations liees a la tache sur une cohorte est une technique novatrice qui permettra d'apporter de nouveaux elements a la comprehension du declin cognitif pathologique. Si les hyperactivations sont presentes avant les symptomes cognitifs, elles pourraient servir d'indicateur precoce du declin cognitif et permettre des interventions avant l'apparition des symptomes.

column36: Impact de la modalite de transport sur l'activite physique globale, la participation sociale et le bien-etre
column37: La societe moderne est caracterisee par la presence de l'automobile. De 1978 en 2016, les statistiques de la Societe de l'assurance automobile du Quebec demontraient une augmentation plus importante du volume de vehicules de promenade par rapport a l'augmentation du nombre de titulaire de permis de conduire. L'utilisation de l'automobile est associee a des impacts de sante, tel que la pollution atmospherique, le bruit et les traumatismes associes aux collisions. Un quatrieme element de sante a considerer est celui de l'inactivite physique. Il existe des solutions alternatifs au transport automobile, tel que le transport collectif, le velo et la marche. Comment la modalite de transport principal vers le milieu de travail des individus conditionne les autres deplacements? Quel est l'impact de ce mode de deplacement sur l'activite physique global, sur la participation sociale et sur le bien-etre? Mon projet de recherche tentera d'explorer ces questions a partir de donnees issus du projet de recherche INTERACT. Impliquant quatre villes canadiennes, dont Montreal, le projet INTERACT mesure notamment la geolocalisation, le deplacement et le mode de transport utilise en temps reel de ses participants dans le but, entre autres, d'evaluer l'effet de la modification de l'environnement urbain sur l'activite physique, la participation sociale et le bien-etre. La particularite de mon projet de recherche est qu'il met en relation la globalite de l'activite physique, le bien-etre et la participation selon le mode de transport principal. L'utilisation de telles donnees est possible par le soutien du projet INTERACT.

column36: An Index of the physical and mental health of Indigenous youth and young adults in the Okanagan.
column37: Currently, very little is known about the physical and mental health of Indigenous youth and young adults living in Canada. Studies show that this population suffers from obesity at an increased rate and children of Indigenous people's are also found to experience greater levels of anxiety and other emotional issues. Research has shown that those young people who spend the most amount of time engaging in sedentary activities and screen time have the lowest levels of health-related quality of life and, subsequently, suffer from obesity and obesity-related disorders at increased rates than the general public. For this reason, it is instrumental to further understand how factors such as sedentary activity and screen time affect important health outcomes such as Health-related quality of life, obesity, and psychological well-being. I will look at the inter-relationships between sedentary behavior, physical activity, sleep, weight status, health-related quality of life, and psychological well-being in off-reserve Indigenous youth and young adults by identifying clusters of health behaviors that determine health-related quality of life and psychological well-being. I will also compare cluster membership between off-reserve indigenous 8- 25 year old's with age- and sex-matched Canadian children. We will be working with our local School District, universities, friendship centers, Metis Associations, and youth groups, to recruit 100 Indigenous young people for this cross-sectional study. Anthropometric measures of weight status will be taken. Sleep, sedentary time, and physical activity will be assessed using an accelerometer/inclinometer worn for one week. This study is an important first step in understanding health determinants in the young off-reserve Indigenous population

column36: Metabolic Syndrome and Endometrial Cancer Survival
column37: For women in Canada, endometrial cancer is the fourth most commonly diagnosed cancer with 7,300 cases diagnosed annually and 1,150 women expected to die from this cancer in 2018. Between 2000 and 2010, Canadian endometrial cancer survival rates decreased 1% annually and women living with obesity, diabetes and/or high blood pressure had less favorable outcomes. Yet, the combined effect of these risk factors on endometrial cancer survivorship is still not well understood. The Metabolic Syndrome (MetS) is the clustering of risk factors including high blood pressure, blood glucose, central adiposity, abnormal cholesterol and triglycerides. To date, only one previous study has explored the effects of the MetS on endometrial cancer survival and reported that women with MetS had 1.56 times the risk of dying from endometrial cancer compared to those who did not have this syndrome. We have identified an association between MetS and endometrial cancer risk. There is biologic plausibility that MetS could also be associated with survival, which remains to be tested. The current study aims to examine the impact of MetS on survival outcomes in endometrial cancer survivors, primarily cancer recurrence, endometrial cancer-specific survival and all-cause mortality. A secondary aim is to examine the association between each component of MetS on these survival outcomes. It is important to identify opportunities to intervene in this population given the decreasing endometrial cancer-specific survival rates. This research will provide additional evidence needed to develop and assess interventions in endometrial cancer survivors targeting early indicators of cardiovascular and metabolic disease, such as MetS, with the ultimate aim of improving endometrial cancer survival.

column36: Mental Heath in Canadian Police: The Role of Gender
column37: The proposed research is designed to investigate gender differences in mental disorder symptoms among Canadian police officer. While police work is associated with increased rates of mental health injuries such as post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), depression, and anxiety, women may be particularly vulnerable. Policewomen often encounter bias, discrimination, and harassment based on their gender and might feel the need to adjust their behaviour to fit both stereotypes of being an officer and being a woman. Understanding police perceptions of being a woman in a service predominantly composed of men may be critical for improving their work environment, supporting the mental health of all officers, and developing focused interventions. The proposed research includes two primary foci of activity. First, quantitative analyses will be conducted to evaluate gender differences in positive screens for mental health disorders (i.e., PTSD, depression, anxiety, and alcohol use disorder) among police officers. Second, interviews will be conducted with equal amounts of policemen and policewomen to explain or expand on quantitative results. These interviews will be focused on the experiences, demands, and coping resources of Canadian police officers. Specifically, investigating which factors might differentiate men and women in their experience navigating the inner and outer demands of police work. This will allow for a necessarily nuanced examination of what factors might differentiate men and women in their mental health symptoms in a higher-risk population, offering opportunities to develop tailored and focused interventions. This research also allows to examine the impacts of gender on health, specifically in policing, where little research has focused in women's experiences.

column36: Canadian Healthy Infant Longitudinal Development (CHILD) Study multi-exposure correlation structures incorporating environmental and microbiome data.
column37: Asthma is the most common chronic childhood disease, impacting 1 in 7 Canadian children. There is recent compelling evidence linking asthma to gut microbiome imbalances linked with environmental factors. However, environmental exposures and subsequent microbiome changes are dynamic, multi-dimensional and potentially interacting. The Canadian Healthy Infant Longitudinal Development (CHILD) study is Canada's largest phenotyped birth cohort, with >31,000 variables and 32 million data points recorded for >3000 children, at 9 time points over their first 8 years. The Brinkman Lab at Simon Fraser University has been leading the creation of the CHILDdb.ca database to store and integrate the CHILD Study data. This study aims to identify early life microbiome-based biomarkers and environmental exposures that predict the risk of future asthma and associated diseases. However, these factors are dynamic and potentially interacting in complex ways. My project aims to use and modify code from Patel and Manrai to create Exposome Globes that can reveal the correlation structures among the different exposures under study. This project will combine the data available from the CHILDdb with CANUE.ca geospatial environmental exposure data. In addition, data of microbial taxa will be incorporated to explore the correlation structures of environmental factors with these taxa. I will compare all of this data with parallel Globes I create from other cohort data from collaborators in the Netherlands and Hong Kong, to identify differences which may help guide any cohort integration. These models will ultimately lead to hypotheses regarding the complexities of these interactions and guide further development of risk factor indices for health outcomes that utilize exposome and microbiome data.
