column36: Investigating the role of Fusobacterium nucleatum and other oncomicrobes in colorectal cancer
column37: Fusobacterium nucleatum is an anaerobic bacterium that is ubiquitous in the human oral cavity, but has been isolated from extra-oral body sites in numerous diseased states. F. nucleatum has been implicated in a broad range of infections and diseases, such as colorectal cancer. This bacterial species has several virulence determinants, including the ability to adhere to and invade human cells, such as colon carcinomas.The purpose of my research is to elucidate the colorectal cancer-promoting role of F. nucleatum, and to investigate the suitability of the murine model for F. nucleatum-associated human colorectal cancer. I hypothesize that equivalent representative murine and human cell lines will exhibit similar cancer-promoting gene expression when infected with F. nucleatum. Additionally, I hypothesize that the host cell response is modulated by the surrounding colon microbiome. My first objective is to characterize the modulation in gene expression of both F. nucleatum and noncancerous human host cells by dual RNA-seq bioinformatics (where fusobacterial and host mRNA are sequenced in tandem). My second objective is to determine the modulation in gene expression of both F. nucleatum and noncancerous murine host cell lines that parallel the noncancerous human cell lines, also by dual RNA-seq. My third objective is to determine whether F. nucleatum works synergistically with other "oncomicrobes"-microbes associated with oncogenesis-and if F. nucleatum can be antagonized by members of the normal colonic microbiota. This objective will be investigated by analyzing the gene expression of both multi-bacterial species infections of host cells, and by infecting host cells with F. nucleatum in the presence of metabolites derived from representative healthy gut microbiomes.

column36: Investigating a Kinase as a Target for Alzheimer's Disease
column37: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common form of dementia, accounting for 60-70 percent of the approximately 50 million dementia cases worldwide, as reported by the World Health Organization. Patients experiencing the neurodegeneration associated with this disease do not have treatment options that interfere with disease progression; current treatments only alleviate symptoms. This project will investigate the protein calcium/calmodulin dependant protein kinase 1 delta (CaMK1D) as a novel target for late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD). Several studies have linked CaMK1D to AD, including genetic studies and studies examining the amount of CaMK1D and specific fragments of CaMK1D in the brains of AD patients. Here, three main hypotheses will be explored. First, that CaMK1D is modified, cut into smaller pieces, and hyperactive during AD. Second, that the hyperactivity of CaMK1D leads to modification of other AD related proteins to resemble their state in AD, and lastly, the use of specific inhibitors for CaMK1D can control the progression of AD type pathology in cell culture. To explore these hypotheses, neuronal cell culture methods that mimic the AD state biochemically will be used as a model. Determination of the state and function of CaMK1D in AD models, as well as its contribution to AD pathways, represents a new strategy for stopping progression of AD.

column36: Awake 2-photon Imaging of an Alzheimer's Disease Rat Model
column37: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease accounting for the majority of dementia cases. The disease is categorized by accumulation of extracellular amyloid plaques and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles. Symptoms of disease include speech difficulties, memory deficits, and eventual impairments to basic life functions due to widespread neuronal loss. Neurons are the basic functional cells within the brain and require oxygen and glucose from the blood for activity and survival. AD disrupts the delivery of reagents to the brain and this is referred to as defective neurovascular coupling. Most studies have examined neurovascular coupling in mouse models under anesthesia. Confounding those studies is the fact that anesthesia modulates the delivery of blood to the brain. Additionally, mice models do not completely recapitulate symptoms of the disease. An advanced microscopy technique is used to study neurovascular coupling. This technique is a very powerful microscope that can be used to simultaneously monitor neurons activation and changes to the blood vessels near them. Tg-F344-AD is a rat model which recapitulates age-dependent nature of AD exhibiting amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles leading to frank neuronal loss. This study will use Tg-F344-AD rat model to examine neurovascular coupling within a specific region of the brain called medial prefrontal cortex while awake. I hypothesize there will be an age- and disease-dependent decline in neurovascular coupling response. This study will be the first of its kind to examine the medial prefrontal cortex in AD within the context of an awake animal model. It would aid in our understanding of AD without confounding variables such as anesthesia which disrupt normal brain physiology.

column36: Prediction assistee par intelligence artificielle des sequelles des commotions cerebrales du sport depuis la ligne de touche : est-ce que la sciences des donnees sera mise sur la ligne de touche par les protagonistes des sports de contact ?
column37: Au Quebec tout comme aux Etats-Unis, les commotions cerebrales liees a la pratique sportive sont un probleme de sante publique. Au moment de l'accident, les outils de depistage disponibles pour l'equipe d'intervenants medicaux sont bases sur l'observation de symptomes pour justifier le retrait et le retour au jeu d'un athlete. Malgre des annees de perfectionnement, l'approche basee sur les symptomes cliniques post-commotionnels s'avere dangereuse en raison du faux sentiment de securite qu'elle procure. D'ailleurs, les athletes sont plutot enclins a minimiser leurs symptomes afin de retourner rapidement au jeu. Ce programme de recherche se distingue en offrant une alternative se basant sur des parametres objectifs et quantifiables de l'integrite cerebrale par l'entremise de techniques de neuroimagerie avancee et des proprietes biomecaniques des coups portes a la tete. L'objectif de cette etude est de modeliser, pour la premiere fois, les modifications de l'integrite du cerveau engendrees par l'application de forces portees a la tete lors d'un contact durant un match chez des joueurs de football universitaires. Ultimement, cette modelisation basee sur l'intelligence artificielle fournira une analyse en temps reel du risque d'un athlete de presenter des lesions cerebrales a la suite d'un coup a la tete en s'appuyant sur les forces d'acceleration enregistrees a partir du casque. Cette modelisation permettra que la prise de decision quant au retrait du jeu d'un joueur soit basee sur des donnees objectives de risque de dommage au cerveau, plutot que sur des symptomes subjectifs, auto-rapportes par l'athlete.

column36: Advance Care Planning and The Law
column37: Everyone deserves the opportunity to share their personal values, and preferences for future medical care with their loved ones and health care providers (HCPs). However, many Canadians are unprepared for their own or their families decline in health. When medical crises occur, most people have not planned for who will make decisions if they cannot, nor what decisions they would want those persons to make. As a result, families face uncertainty, often deciding on life support treatments for their loved ones. HCPs are ill-equipped to navigate these complexities and often experience them as ethical rather than legal issues. Advance care planning (ACP) ensures that patients receive the medical care they want, during chronic and serious illness, and when they are unable to speak for themselves. This on-ongoing, shared decision-making communication process supports adults, healthy and not, to think and prepare for their future health care. Currently, there is limited uptake of ACP in Canada and HCPs struggle with their roles and responsibilities in the process. The primary objective of this research is to explore HCPs understanding of legal requirements and obligations imposed by BC law throughout the ACP process. Interviews will be held with ACP leaders who have experience developing ACP training and support. The secondary objective is to identify key factors contributing to successfully implementing ACP and provide sustainable solutions. Using a qualitative case study approach, this project will explore how the obligations imposed by law impact HCPs ability to support patients and families through the ACP processes. This study will be the first in BC and Canada to provide insights and offer solutions to these complex issues arising at end of life.

column36: Impact de l'infiltration bacterienne intra-tumorale sur la reponse immunitaire et la survie des individus atteints du cancer du sein.
column37: Au Canada, le cancer du sein est la deuxieme cause de deces lies au cancer. L'immunotherapie est une arme revolutionnaire contre le cancer qui consiste a stimuler notre propre systeme immunitaire pour que le corps elimine les cellules cancereuses. Cependant, cette approche ne fonctionne pas encore de facon optimale en cancer du sein. Il a recemment ete decouvert que la prise de medicaments contre les infections bacteriennes, les antibiotiques, bloquait l'efficacite des immunotherapies. La prise d'antibiotiques en prevention semble donc debalancer l'equilibre des bacteries de l'intestin qui ont une importance dans l'effet anti-cancer du systeme immunitaire. Les bacteries du systeme digestif intriguent les scientifiques puisque celles-ci ont des effets importants sur la sante humaine. Contrairement a ce qu'on croyait, les bacteries ne se limitent pas qu'au systeme digestif, elles sont presentes dans plusieurs organes. Nous savons que les seins possedent leurs propres bacteries, mais leur presence et diversite dans la tumeur est inconnue. Le but poursuivi dans ce projet est d'identifier les bacteries presentes dans le cancer du sein, d'evaluer leur nombre, puis d'etudier leur effet sur le systeme immunitaire. Pour ce faire, la tumeur est observee afin de determiner si des globules blancs specialises dans l'elimination du cancer, les lymphocytes T, sont entres en presence de bacteries. Ensuite, les donnees cliniques des patientes sont utilisees pour determiner si la presence de bacteries dans la tumeur ameliore la survie. L'administration dans la tumeur de bacteries identifiees pour leurs effets benefiques sur la reponse anti-tumorale du systeme immunitaire permettra d'ameliorer le succes des traitements actuels et la survie des individus atteints du cancer du sein.

column36: Trouble disruptif avec dysregulation emotionnelle, depression, desespoir, suicidalite et traits borderline chez des adolescents en milieu clinique
column37: Le DSM-5 presente un nouveau diagnostic chez l'enfant et l'adolescent?; le trouble disruptif avec dysregulation emotionnelle (TDDE). Il se caracterise par de l'irritabilite chronique, entrainant plusieurs crises de colere par semaine. Althoff (2016), indique que les adolescents ayant un TDDE rapportent plus d'ideations et de comportements suicidaires que les jeunes ayant une autre psychopathologie. De plus, le TDDE est associe a un risque eleve de trouble depressif au debut de l'age adulte (Brotman et al., 2006). L'impulsivite liee a la colere, la suicidalite et la gestion difficile de l'humeur sont trois elements qui rejoignent le trouble de personnalite borderline. Toutefois, a notre connaissance, aucune recherche ne fait encore le lien entre le TDDE et les traits borderline. Afin de faciliter l'identification du TDDE, Breton, Bergeron et Labelle (2011) ont construit une echelle de depistage qui a ete distribuee a Montreal dans diverses cliniques. Aussi, plusieurs recherches ont propose des traitements psychologiques pour le TDDE. Toutefois, il n'existe pas de consensus a ce niveau. Ce projet vise a determiner dans quelle mesure le TDDE est lie a la depression, au desespoir, a la suicidalite et aux traits borderline et a recenser les differents traitements afin de determiner les meilleures pratiques. Les 192 participants ages de 12 a 15 ans ont complete plusieurs instruments psychometriques mesurant toutes les variables a l'etude. Des analyses bivariees permettront d'observer la force du lien entre le TDDE et les autres concepts. Une revue systematique portera sur les traitements psychologiques proposes pour le TDDE. Ainsi, reconnaitre et definir le TDDE a l'adolescence permettra de favoriser la prevention du suicide et de pathologies ayant une incidence a vie.

column36: Networks of Resilience: Studying the Pitfalls, Perils, and Pathways to Participatory Processes
column37: This research is based on the premise that Canadians are potentially stuck at a dangerous intersection of disaster risk and citizen apathy, and that solutions to gaps in local-level disaster and emergency management planning can be found within the collective voices of community networks. As a potential network of resilience, how can a community-based health network influence local-level Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR)? In partnering with a network that fosters collaborative partnerships around the social determinants of health (SDoH), this research is uniquely positioned to build awareness of the connections between underlying vulnerabilities related to SDoH and the drivers of disaster risk and community resilience. Using participatory action research and social network analysis methods to measure the network strengths, gaps, and opportunities, this research aims to convey how place-based vulnerability and resilience data might create collaborative knowledge transmission opportunities to explore the local-level linkages between SDoH and DRR. This new knowledge can further support the network in extending an invitation to community partners and stakeholders to collaboratively generate ideas for local initiatives that can build from the identified strengths of the network to address identified gaps and contribute to improved health and disaster outcomes simultaneously.

column36: Myosin phosphatase rho-interacting protein mediates DDR1-dependent collagen contraction
column37: The extracellular matrix (ECM) is the structural component of tissues and organs that provides tissue-resident cells with critical signals that regulate their function and fate. The most abundant structural component of the ECM is collagen, a fibrillar protein. Like other ECM components, collagen is continuously recycled by a complex, multistep remodeling process. Failure to maintain balanced remodeling is associated with diseases such as cancer and the fibrosis of heart failure. In cancer, dysfunctional collagen remodeling surrounding tumors is associated with both cancer progression and metastasis. In cardiac fibrosis, excessive collagen is deposited in the heart wall and can ultimately lead to heart failure. Collagen is usually remodeled by cells through cellular connectors called adhesion receptors, that attach the internal cell skeleton to collagen fibers. Previous research showed the critical role played by an adhesion receptor (DDR1) in binding and remodeling collagen. Our lab discovered that DDR1 links collagen with the cell skeleton by binding to a protein (myosin) which is located inside the cell. Myosin enables the skeleton of the cell to contract and generate forces that are transmitted through DDR1 to the collagen network, which is critical for tissue remodeling. Our study aims to investigate how DDR1 and myosin work together to remodel collagen. Preliminary results indicate that MRIP, a protein that regulates myosin contraction, also attaches to DDR1 and may regulate the DDR1-myosin interaction. An improved understanding of the interplay between DDR1, MRIP, and myosin, will show us how disruptions of collagen remodeling can lead to diseases such as cancer and heart failure, and then suggest possible strategies for better prevention and treatment.

column36: Is Delirium Associated with Depression and Anxiety in Caregivers of the Critically Ill?
column37: Family caregivers are important partners during and after a patient's stay in the intensive care unit (ICU). Caregivers who visit patients in the ICU may witness delirium, a medical state of confusion that impacts 45-87% of ICU patients. Seeing delirium can be very distressing; for example, caregivers who witnessed delirium in palliative care patients were 12 times more likely to have symptoms of anxiety compared to caregivers who had not. It is important to understand how delirium plays a role in caregiver depression and anxiety, and whether caregivers continue to face these burdens after the patient has returned home. This project is a prospective cohort study nested within a randomized controlled trial that is recruiting caregivers of patients in Foothills Medical Centre medical-surgical ICU (Calgary, Alberta) and measures symptoms of depression, anxiety, and delirium using the Patient Health Questionnaire 9-Item (PHQ-9), Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7-Item (GAD-7), and the Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist (ICDSC), respectively. We aim to see how the number of new and existing cases of depression and anxiety in ICU caregivers compares to the general population. We will also see if caregivers of patients with delirium are more likely to have depression and anxiety. Caregiver depression and anxiety will be measured for a maximum of 5 ICU-days and at 3- and 6-months after the patient leaves the ICU to see if these symptoms continue. This study will be the first to evaluate patient delirium and caregiver depression and anxiety in an ICU setting. With Canada's aging population and projected 80% increase in ICU admissions by 2026, it is crucial that we address delirium as a factor that may significantly impact the mental health in Canadian ICU caregivers.

column36: Stress des enfants durant la transition du prescolaire au scolaire : Le role du cortisol dans le developpement des troubles de sante mentale
column37: Sachant que 50% des maladies mentales apparaissent avant l'age de 14 ans, il est important d'identifier un mecanisme precoce de vulnerabilite. D'ailleurs, il a ete observe que la sante mentale pouvait etre associee a une exposition elevee ou prolongee au stress mesure par l'hormone cortisol. Par ailleurs, il a ete demontre que la transition du prescolaire au scolaire, consideree comme un stresseur social universel, est associee a une augmentation du niveau de cortisol, malgre des differences individuelles importantes. Des recherches ont egalement demontre un lien entre le cortisol et les troubles interiorises ainsi qu'entre le cortisol et un temperament inhibe. Ce projet de recherche aura donc 3 objectifs : (a) dresser un patron de la reaction cortisolaire lors de la transition du prescolaire au scolaire; (b) observer si des reactions cortisolaires atypiques sont liees a des difficultes de sante mentale et si ce lien differe selon le sexe; (c) identifier les facteurs de vulnerabilite a des reactions cortisolaires atypiques. Plus particulierement, il sera determine, selon differents patrons de reactions, si des reactions cortisolaires atypiques sont liees a des troubles interiorises et dans quelle mesure le temperament inhibe sera moderateur de ces reactions. Pour ce faire, des donnees d'un projet en cours de collecte suivant environ 400 enfants de la prematernelle a la 2e annee du primaire seront utilisees. En bref, cette etude permettra de mieux comprendre l'experience et l'ampleur de la reaction de stress des enfants lors de la transition scolaire ainsi que son implication fonctionnelle. Ceci facilitera alors le developpement d'outils de depistage ou de prevention precoce, car l'entree scolaire constitue un moment privilegie pour le depistage systematique precoce.

column36: Natural Antisense Transcripts and Their Potential as Toxoplasmosis Drug Targets
column37: Toxoplasma gondii is a parasitic protozoan that causes Toxoplasmosis, a disease that affects more than half of the world's population and is a leading cause of death in immunocompromised humans. Despite the prevalence and medical significance of Toxoplasmosis, there is currently no cure for this disease. To develop effective treatments for Toxoplasmosis, biomolecules involved in cellular processes of T. gondii often serve as good targets for drug discoveries. A gene important for T. gondii growth and virulence, known as the ubiquitin-like protease 1 (Ulp1), was found to be controlled by a transcription unit on the opposite strand referred to as the Ulp1-Natural Antisense Transcript (Ulp1-NAT). To examine whether Ulp1-NAT affects T. gondii growth and virulence by regulating Ulp1, CRISPR Intereference (CRISPRi) is used for analysis along with replication and plaque assays. By studying how the Ulp1-NAT controls Ulp1 and its resulting impact on parasite fitness, efficacious drugs for treating Toxoplasmosis can be created and put an end to this global threat.

column36: Informations perceptuelles utilisees lors de la planification et du contournement d'une personne et l'impact du vieillissement sur les informations utilisees.
column37: Contourner une personne en mouvement est une activite quotidienne encore mal comprise. Selon le peu de connaissance a ce sujet, on sait que la complexite de cette tache implique certaines differences entre les jeunes adultes et les personnes agees dans sa planification et son execution. Toutefois, la facon dont les informations visuelles de l'autre personne sont utilisees ainsi que l'impact du vieillissement pour contourner une autre personne restent incompris. L'objectif principal de ce projet est de comprendre les informations que nous utilisons par rapport aux mouvements des autres pour les contourner dans une situation sociale, incluant l'influence du vieillissement. Notre hypothese est que l'information des mouvements corporelles d'un autre permettra de mieux planifier le contournement et que les resultats seront plus variables pour les personnes agees. Pour ce faire, 20 jeunes adultes et 20 personnes de 70 ans et plus habitant dans la communaute sans probleme de sante seront recrutes. Ils seront immerges dans un environnement virtuel representant un centre commercial. Le but des participants sera d'entrer dans un magasin situe devant eux. column36: Is natural folate as effective as synthetic folic acid in increasing plasma and red blood cell folate concentrations during pregnancy? A proof-of-concept pilot study
column37: Adequate folate status in early pregnancy is associated with prevention of neural tube defects (NTD). For this reason, Health Canada recommends pregnant women consume 0.4-1 mg/day of folic acid. Folic acid is a synthetic, man-made source of folate. A recently developed form of natural folate (Metafolin) is gaining popularity in Canada. It is being used increasingly in prenatal multivitamins, but has never been evaluated in pregnancy. Natural folate and folic acid are metabolized differently. Natural folate can enter circulation directly, whereas folic acid must be converted to folate through a series of steps. Recent evidence suggests that humans cannot convert such large doses of folic acid. In amounts as low as 0.2 mg/day, there is a build-up of unmetabolized folic acid in the blood, which has been associated with acceleration of some cancers and altered DNA development. Thus, natural folate may be safer for pregnant women and their babies than synthetic folic acid. We aim to test whether supplementation with natural folate can increase blood folate levels to at least 906nmol/L, a level associated with a very low risk of NTDs. Second, we aim to test if supplementation with natural folate results in lower unmetabolized folic acid levels, as compared to synthetic folic acid. We will randomize 60 healthy pregnant women to 0.6 mg folic acid or natural folate for 16 weeks. We will initiate the trial in later pregnancy, after neural tube closure, to reduce the risk of harm should the natural folate prove less effective. We will measure levels of serum folate, red blood cell folate, and unmetabolized folic acid. This proof-of-concept trial is the first step in determining the safest and most effective form of folate supplements for Canadian women and their babies.

column36: Effect of cognitively engaging physical activity on executive functions in children
column37: Plenty of research has shown physical activity is beneficial for the physical, emotional, and mental health of children. Studies report it can even increase brain functioning. For example, we know that children who are more fit are more likely to be successful in school. Some types of physical activities (e.g. soccer) require more thinking than others (e.g. walking), and it is thought that physical activities that require more thinking can have greater benefits on brain functioning. The goal of this study was to determine whether combining physical activity and thinking in a fun game can improve brain function in children who are 11-12 years old. We are going to assess how fit children are prior to the study to see if their baseline fitness affects brain functioning, and we will be asking children how they are feeling throughout the study. We expect that children who are assigned to do physical activity that requires thinking will show greater increases in brain functioning and positive emotions than groups that do physical activity or thinking tasks alone, and that children who were more fit to begin with will show greater increases in brain functioning. Children participating in this study will be scheduled for two visits at the University of Toronto. In visit one, we will ask children to perform some fitness assessments. In visit two, children will be randomly assigned to either (1) Physical activity that requires thinking, where children will play a life-sized game of Connect 4, (2) Physical activity only, where children won't use thinking skills, and (3) Cognitive only, where children will play a seated game of Connect 4. Before and after the activity, we will ask children how they are feeling, and we will give them 3 games to do that assess brain functioning.

column36: The Efficacy of Postnatal Choline Supplementation on Reversing Deficits in Hippocampal Plasticity Induced by Prenatal Ethanol Exposure
column37: Consuming alcohol during pregnancy causes a range of lifelong effects on the offspring, known as Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (FASD). Recent research has explored supplementing the essential nutrient choline to mitigate the associated cognitive deficits. These studies have seen promising results when measuring behavioural outcomes in both animal studies of prenatal ethanol exposure (PNEE) and in clinical trials. However, little is understood of the mechanisms behind this treatment. This study will use a rodent model of FASD to elucidate changes within the hippocampus, an area of the brain vital to memory consolidation. Memories are formed from the strengthening of neuronal synapses, a process known as long term potentiation (LTP). LTP is modulated by cholinergic inputs, acetylcholine producing neurons, and alteration of these circuits may be one mechanism in which choline rescues cognitive impairments. Offspring will be exposed to ethanol throughout the gestational period, with 35.5% of the caloric intake derived from ethanol. Choline treatment will begin on postnatal day 10. Hippocampal-dependent behavioural tasks will validate that choline rescues memory deficits in this model of PNEE. Electrophysiological recordings in the dentate gyrus of the hippocampus will elucidate changes on a molecular level, specifically to determine if choline enhances LTP in PNEE animals. Additionally, pharmaceutical agents that block cholinergic receptors or stimulate their activity will confirm that the modulation of LTP is dependent on local changes in choline activity. Together, these experiments will further define the mechanisms behind postnatal choline supplementation and provide molecular evidence for the rescuing of cognitive impairments in this potential treatment of FASD.

column37: Plusieurs conditions genetiques, dont le syndrome du X-fragile (SXF), la sclerose tubereuse de Bourneville (STB) et les syndromes aux mutations du gene PTEN, sont associees a un fort risque d'epilepsie. L'epilepsie est une manifestation clinique liee a un desequilibre entre les mecanismes excitateurs et inhibiteurs du cerveau. Toutefois, l'epilepsie, dans ces conditions, est souvent resistante aux traitements pharmacologiques. Il devient donc necessaire de definir les alterations precises dans le desequilibre excitation/inhibition chez ces patients afin d'optimiser le traitement de leurs anomalies neurologiques. A cet egard, la stimulation magnetique transcranienne (SMT) offre l'opportunite unique d'investiguer de facon non invasive les principaux mecanismes d'inhibition et d'excitation intracorticaux chez l'humain. Ainsi, l'objectif principal de ce projet est de caracteriser le profil neurophysiologique des personnes avec le SXF, la STB et les syndromes aux mutations du gene PTEN quant a l'inhibition et l'excitation intracorticale. Pour ce faire, 20 enfants ayant une de ces conditions genetiques, ainsi que 20 enfants sans probleme neurologique, seront recrutes. Les participants seront tous ages entre 7 et 18 ans. Leur profil neuropsychologique sera evalue afin de deceler, notamment, la presence de deficience intellectuelle. De plus, une batterie d'evaluation par SMT sera utilisee pour etablir l'integrite des mecanismes inhibiteurs et excitateurs du cerveau.

column37: Afin de retarder le developpement de la maladie d'Alzheimer, la recherche doit miser sur des interventions precoces et preventives aupres d'individus avec un trouble neurocognitif leger (TCL), qui correspond a un prodrome, probable de la maladie. Comme alternative a l'approche pharmacologique, ce projet mise sur une intervention basee sur la meditation pleine conscience (IBPC). Elle consiste a porter une attention stable et sans jugement sur une experience qui se vit dans le moment present. Le projet actuel vise a ameliorer les fonctions cognitives, comme l'attention et la memoire, en plus d'ameliorer la sante psychologique, par la reduction des symptomes depressifs et anxieux et le stress percu par la personne agee avec un TCL. Une intervention active de psychoeducation sera utilisee comme point de comparaison pour les effets de l'IBPC. Une fois les donnees analysees a l'aide de modeles mixtes et autres analyses statistiques, les resultats attendus sont une amelioration de la memoire et de l'attention, une diminution des symptomes depressifs, anxieux et de stress percu, une augmentation de la qualite de vie et du bien-etre et une augmentation de la capacite a exercer la pleine conscience. Les analyses visent egalement a comprendre les relations entre ces variables a l'aide d'analyses de mediation et de moderation. Ce projet sera le premier a demontrer les impacts benefiques holistiques d'une IBPC pour les personnes avec un TCL avec symptomes anxieux et depressifs. Elle est susceptible de produire des effets globaux qui auront un impact important sur la qualite de vie et la condition de sante des participants. Le projet s'insere dans un courant relativement recent de prise en charge non pharmacologique du prodrome de la maladie d'Alzheimer.

column36: Reporting of Financial Conflicts of Interest in Meta-Analyses of Pharmacological Treatment Trials: A Cross-sectional Study
column37: Financial conflicts of interest (COI) are present in situations where a financial interest has the potential to influence a primary interest, for example evaluating the effectiveness of a drug. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses synthesize information from multiple studies and are considered one of the strongest sources of scientific evidence. The failure to report financial COI from the studies included in systematic reviews and meta-analyses may lead readers to believe that COI were not present or not important. As a result, readers are prevented from determining whether financial COI may have influenced the findings. Previous studies have shown that systematic reviews and meta-analyses of drugs often fail to report COI from included randomized controlled trials. However, these studies were conducted in 2011-2012 and examined high-impact journals, which are known for their rigor, and may not be representative of reporting practices more generally or of current practices. The objectives of my project are to (1) evaluate the extent to which meta-analyses of drugs report COI from included trials in large sample not restricted to high impact journals and (2) to examine factors associated with reporting COI from trials included in meta-analyses. To achieve this, I will extract data on factors that may influence whether COI from included trials are reported, such as meta-analysis funding sources and journal impact factor. Following this, variables will be entered into a regression model to determine which factors are associated with the reporting of COI from included trials. This study has the potential to improve medical decision-making by helping researchers and health care professionals to accurately assess the potential for bias from COI in meta-analyses.

column36: Essential role of clathrin signalosomes in receptor signaling in cancer cells.
column37: Cells communicate with each other through chemical cues, each of which can trigger a specific cell response. For instance, epidermal growth factor (EGF) elicits a cellular response when it binds to epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). EGFR is a receptor on the cell surface that controls much of what cells can do such as growth, movement (migration) and survival. Therefore, EGFR must be tightly regulated by the cell. When this control fails, this can lead to growth, survival and metastasis of many tumors. Our lab has identified a new function for the protein clathrin inside cells to control the function of EGFR and thus its ability to control cell growth and survival. Clathrin forms tiny structures that are a few nanometers long, that critically also contain other proteins called TOM1L1 and Fyn. These tiny clathrin structure are critical to control EGFR; however, we do not fully understand how these dynamic protein assemblies form, and how specifically they are able to control the oncogene EGFR. To better understand how clathrin controls EGFR, I will use fluorescently-tagged versions of the key proteins clathrin, TOM1L1 and Fyn alongside labelled EGFR in living cancer cells, coupled to advanced microscopy. Using this and computer-based automated image analysis, I will learn how clathrin protein assemblies control the key oncogene EGFR in certain cancers. The significance of this research is that understanding this novel role of clathrin has the potential to reveal new weakness of certain cancers that can be thus targeted with new drugs.

column36: A Temporal Trend and Risk Factor Analysis of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius Isolates from Dogs in Atlantic Canada
column37: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in many bacterial pathogens has become a widespread issue and a significant threat to the treatment of infectious diseases in both humans and animals. Today, Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius (MRSP), is a common cause of infections in adult dogs, particularly skin infections. A retrospective analysis of the Atlantic Veterinary College Diagnostic Services Bacteriology Laboratory and the Atlantic Veterinary Teaching Hospital medical records will be performed. The area of AMR is one of the key health issues of interest highlighted by the Canadian Association of Veterinary Medicine, the Canadian Food Inspection Agency, and the Public Health Agency of Canada. This research will contribute to the understanding of AMR trends and risk factors in companion animals associated with MRSP and the potential risk of exposure of MRSP to humans. column36: Network Analysis for Modeling Multimorbidity in Administrative Data
column37: Multimorbidity, the presence of two or more chronic medical conditions, results in poorer health outcomes, including lower quality of life, for those that experience it. Today, more people are living with multimorbidity than ever because of an aging population and increasing rates of certain chronic diseases and their risk factors, like obesity. This makes reducing and managing multimorbidity a very important task for Canadians. In addition to improving quality of life, reducing multimorbidity will considerably reduce government spending on healthcare services. This project will look at the types of chronic conditions that cluster together, to better understand profiles of multimorbidity in the population. In order to do this, we will use data for the entire population that is found in administrative health records (hospital, physician, and prescription records) as well as electronic medical records. The detailed information found in these administrative data will be analyzed using computer rules that identify patterns of chronic conditions in the population. We will experiment with and evaluate different computing techniques for constructing these disease networks. We will also compare the results obtained from administrative data alone to when electronic medical records are incorporated. After completing this research, we will summarize these comparisons so that other researchers could learn from our work. The conclusions we arrive at will lead to recommendations about methods to measure multimorbidity and will guide future multimorbidity research. This research will help to inform disease prevention and management actions, which can lead to cost savings for the Canadian healthcare system and improve the lives of those living with multiple chronic conditions.

column37: La degenerescence maculaire liee a l'age (DMLA) est grandement handicapante: elle entraine habituellement une perte de la vision centrale, ne laissant intacte que la vision peripherique. Jusqu'a ce jour, il n'existe aucun traitement contre la maladie et les patients doivent s'y adapter en utilisant un point de fixation attentionnel en peripherie, une habitude extremement difficile a implanter qui peut demander des annees de travail. Pourtant, les systemes des mouvements oculaires et de l'attention, enormement sollicites dans la vision, sont connus pour etre particulierement plastiques et rapides a entrainer. Les patients ayant la DMLA pourraient grandement beneficier d'un deplacement efficace de leur attention en peripherie, en effectuant des mouvements oculaires adaptes a leur perte de vision. Par ailleurs, il est possible d'entrainer nos saccades, automatiques, a se modifier: c'est l'adaptation saccadique. Cette methode produit des effets en une periode tres courte, effets qui se maintiennent pourtant a long terme. A ce jour, nous ignorons s'il est possible, en l'absence de vision centrale, d'augmenter l'efficacite du traitement visuel par l'adaptation saccadique. En entrainant la modification des saccades en presence d'une tache de discrimination visuelle en peripherie, sans vision centrale, la presente etude pourra explorer cette possibilite. Des personnes agees saines, pour lesquelles la perte de vision centrale sera simulee, et des personnes ayant la DMLA participeront au programme d'entrainement. Si des changements positifs s'observent, cette etude permettra d'etablir des programmes d'intervention efficaces pour ameliorer le traitement visuel chez les patients ayant la DMLA, ce qui aurait un impact majeur sur leur fonctionnement quotidien et leur qualite de vie.

column36: The Tumour Immune Microenvironment in Breast Ductal Carcinoma In Situ Progression to Invasive Cancer
column37: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) comprises around 20% of all breast cancer diagnoses. DCIS, which can be considered as "stage 0 breast cancer", is a collection of abnormal cells lining the ducts of breast tissue and has been shown to increase the likelihood of developing more aggressive and invasive tumours. Not all DCIS progresses to invasive breast cancer, however as of yet there remains no clear method of determining which DCIS lesions are most likely to become invasive, therefore the standard is to treat all patients with wide-local excision surgery, followed by radiotherapy. Thus, there is an urgent need to better be able to predict and prevent disease progression, in order to reduce over-treatment of DCIS. My proposed research is focused on ways to better predict the progression of DCIS and the role of the immune system in tumour growth. The immune system is activated during early cancer development, in an effort to eliminate abnormal cancer cells, but during more advanced stages the immune system is suppressed, and cancer cells tend to acquire the ability to evade immune system surveillance. This process is called immunoediting. Using a DCIS mouse model, I plan to look at how the process of immunoediting can be interrupted, by promoting an overall more activated immune microenvironment. I will also evaluate human paired DCIS and invasive breast cancer tissue using imaging mass cytometry, to gain a more comprehensive overview of the immune microenvironment and how it changes with invasion. The results obtained from this project will contribute to a better understanding of how the immune system modulates breast cancer progression and how this can be used to treat patients with DCIS more appropriately.

column36: Satisfying psychological needs during postoperative orthopedic rehabilitation: Impact of a training for physical therapists on young patients' adherence, health, and well-being
column37: Rehabilitation following a bone surgery is important for a successful recovery. Motivation has been identified as an essential psychological factor in supporting sustained exercise, which in turn is associated with better health outcomes. According to Self-determination theory (SDT), in order to foster one's motivation, a person's three basic psychological needs (BPN) of competence, autonomy, and relatedness must be fulfilled. Competence means that the person is confident in his/her ability to perform a skill. Autonomy refers to perceived behavioural freedom. Relatedness refers to how close and connected a person feels in his/her everyday interactions. Therefore, we will train three physiotherapists (PTs) at the Shriners-Hospitals for Children(R)-Canada to integrate these notions into their practice. Then, we will recruit 100 patients, from the ages of 8 to 21, who had a bone surgery and need physical therapy. We will assign patients to PTs who either had or had not received the training. Participants will not know in which condition they are. We will measure BPN satisfaction, motivation, positive emotions, self-efficacy, and exercise adherence using questionnaires after a month of rehabilitation and once patients will have completed their physical rehabilitation. Patient-specific physical outcomes, such as gains in strength and mobility, will be provided by treating PTs. We will compare the two groups to determine whether, as predicted, the training offered to PTS fosters these physical and psychological health outcomes. This study will inform health care professionals about effective interpersonal approaches to improve young patients' rehabilitation adherence, health, and well-being.

column37: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a devastating illness which results in memory loss, inability to think clearly and other behavior abnormalities. It is thought to be caused by the accumulation of misfolded proteins in the brain, making them unable to conduct electrical signals. However, the exact process through which AD occurs is still largely unknown. Recent work has shown that a certain population of highly specialized cells known as Ependymal cells in the brain tend to accumulate cellular waste as they age, which slows them down. column37: Platelets play essential roles in maintaining hemostasis by adhering to vessel walls, activating, and aggregating. However, the same processes can result in vessel occlusion, which may lead to heart attack and stroke. Prior to vessel occlusion, shear stress at the stenotic area escalates. Here, interactions between the glycoprotein (GP) Ib-IX-V complex on platelet surfaces with von Willebrand factor on the injured vessel walls, play a key role in initiating platelet adhesion - making it a desirable target for novel anti-thrombotic therapies. Previous studies have demonstrated that integrin alphaIIbbeta3 inhibitors (the most abundant platelet adhesion receptor) although effective anti-thrombotic agents, can induce severe bleeding in some patients. Previously, our lab showed that Anfibatide (Anf) - a novel GPIbalpha antagonist - is a potent and safe anti-thrombotic agent. Recently, we observed that at high doses, Anf decreased platelet counts to almost half of initial levels. Interestingly, platelet levels rebounded and recovered to normal at 24 hours. This drug-induced "pseudo thrombocytopenia" has never been reported but understanding this mechanism - which may enhance the anti-thrombotic effect of Anf - is important for the development of Anf as an anti-thrombotic drug. We will assess sequestration of platelets in major organs following Anf delivery. Furthermore, we will assess changes on the surface adhesion molecules of platelets and its thrombogenic capacity following Anf delivery. The results of this project will shed light on the phenomena of platelet sequestration and expand our understanding of the mechanism of action of Anf - ultimately leading to the development of more effective pharmaceutical agents for the treatment of thrombotic cardiovascular diseases.

column36: Coping with Fear of Cancer Recurrence
column37: Fear of cancer recurrence affects many patients, and fear of recurrence occurs across many different types of cancer diagnoses. Fear of recurrence is not only associated with psychological distress and lower quality of life, but has treatment implications as it may influence patients' beliefs about their medication, treatment, illness, and health care usage. My proposed research would like to investigate coping techniques that can reduce fear of cancer recurrence in patients, as uncovering ways to reduce fear of recurrence could lead to relevant and cost-effective clinical interventions. I will be investigating factors associated with fear of cancer recurrence at the beginning of my study, but most importantly, I will be checking in at six and nine months to see if fear of recurrence reduction is associated with any particular coping techniques and factors (or if certain factors and coping techniques increase fear of recurrence). Since fear of cancer recurrence can increase over time, it is important to study this variable at multiple time points to create research that will be most relevant in future clinical interventions. This research will be impactful not only since it has the potential to increase quality of life and reduce psychological suffering in cancer patients, but because reduced fear of recurrence may impact treatment and health care usage. Since the effects of cancer are widespread and well-known, this research has the potential to have far-reaching effects.

column36: Proteomic identification of Alzheimer's Disease biomarkers
column37: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by gradual cognitive decline and deposition of amyloid-beta (A?) plaques and neurofibrillary tangles in the brain. Current clinical practices rely on evaluating clinical symptoms, providing no definitive diagnosis until post-mortem neuropathological confirmation. Additionally, the prevailing biomarkers of AD, A? plaques and tau, cannot reliably resolve disease progression and differential diagnosis. The cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), a proximal fluid to the CNS, offers an ideal reservoir for biomarker discovery, as it reflects biochemical changes in the brain. Preliminary evidence from our laboratory suggests that brain-specific proteins in the CSF, neuropentraxin receptor (NPTXR), A? precursor-like protein 1 (APLP1), and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), are biomarkers of AD. I aim to 1) discover additional CSF biomarkers of AD from 60 brain-specific candidate proteins and 2) validate NPTXR, APLP1, and BDNF as biomarkers of AD using a pool of patient CSF samples with matched controls (n=557). I hypothesize that downregulated NPTXR and BDNF levels combined with upregulated APLP1, in addition to other proteins, will create a biomarker pattern that could serve as a robust readout for monitoring AD. I will perform targeted mass spectrometry of 60 candidate proteins in a cohort of control, MCI and AD patient CSF to generate a multivariate prediction panel using machine-learning algorithms. Next, I will leverage existing patient CSF samples, including longitudinally-followed patients and a gradient of AD severities, to validate NPTXR, APLP1, and BDNF for diagnosis and monitoring AD using ELISA. I will conduct correlation analyses of MMSE score and other clinical parameters with protein abundance.

column36: Validation de la version anglaise du Depistage cognitif de Quebec: un nouvel outil de depistage pour les demences atypiques
column37: L'augmentation drastique de la prevalence des troubles neurocognitifs majeurs, une source importante d'invalidite et d'institutionnalisation, constitue un defi crucial en sante publique. Le depistage precoce des demences atypiques demeure difficile, notamment en raison de l'absence d'outils de depistage adaptes. Ces delais privent le patient de ressources, notamment des options pharmacologiques qui sont efficaces dans les stades legers de la maladie. Le Depistage cognitif de Quebec (DCQ ; dcqtest.org ), concu selon les criteres actualises des demences, a ete valide aupres de 628 participants. Il offre une sensibilite et une specificite dans le depistage des demences atypiques qui sont superieures a celles du Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), considere comme la mesure etalon du depistage cognitif. Le DCQ est divise en cinq index ciblant la memoire, les capacites visuospatiales, les fonctions executives, le langage et le comportement. Depuis sa validation, le DCQ a ete traduit et adapte en anglais. L'objectif de cette etude est de valider le DCQ anglais. Des donnees normatives stratifiees selon l'age et l'education seront obtenues. L'equivalence entre les deux versions, la coherence interne, la fiabilite test-retest et la fiabilite interevaluateur seront egalement evaluees. A cette fin, 200 participants sains anglophones de 50 ans et plus seront recrutes dans dix centres universitaires du Canada et des Etats-Unis. Le DCQ et le MoCA seront administres dans un ordre aleatoire. Notre hypothese est que les qualites psychometriques du DCQ anglais seront semblables a celles du DCQ francais. La validation du DCQ anglais permettra une utilisation plus large de l'outil et contribuera a un diagnostic precoce des demences atypiques, et ce, au Canada et a l'international.

column36: Temporal Epigenetic and Transcriptomic Changes in the Innate and Adaptive Immune Responses in Sepsis
column37: Sepsis is a life-threatening dysregulated immune response to infection associated with organ failure and a high mortality rate. Annually, 5.3 million deaths worldwide and 1 in 18 deaths in Canada involve sepsis. It has been shown that the immune system is overactive at the start of sepsis (a "cytokine storm"), but later on becomes suppressed. The majority of sepsis deaths is attributed to this later immunosuppressive phase which can last weeks to months, since patients' immune systems are unable to respond to future infections. Thus, the focus on sepsis treatment should move to understanding why immunosuppression persists for such a long time. We hypothesize that epigenetic changes (enduring, non-genetic processes that lead to long-term modified gene expression such as histone modifications) in monocytes and T cells play a key role. Our lab has shown that monocytes, a short-lived innate immune cell type, are unable to respond to pathogens appropriately during septic-like conditions through a process called "cellular reprogramming". However, since they are short-lived, monocytes alone cannot explain the long duration of immunosuppression. Thus, longer-lived adaptive immune cells such as T cells are likely to be involved, as they may induce reprogramming in new monocytes or become reprogrammed themselves. By analyzing changes in epigenetic regulation and gene expression of monocytes and T cells collected from septic patients at different time points of the disease progression, we can determine the crucial genes and pathways involved in cellular reprogramming and how they change over time. The results from this approach may be used to identify new drug targets, diagnose patients earlier, or predict patient survival, all of which can improve the care of septic patients.

column36: A multidimensional single-cell approach to understand muscle dystrophy
column37: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) and LAMA2-related Muscular Dystrophy (LAMA2 MD) are rare and devastating genetic disease of childhood manifested by progressive skeletal muscle wasting and ultimately death. In both diseases, muscle undergoes constant cycles of degeneration-regeneration exacerbated by intrinsic muscle stem cell (MuSC) dysfunction and their impaired ability to support long-term regeneration. The overall goal of the project is to use a combination of single-cell transcriptomics (RNA-sequencing) and proteomics (mass cytometry, CyTOF) to define the cellular composition of diseased muscle tissues at the single-cell resolution. We will delineate the different cell populations that pre-exist and arise during disease progression and classify the novel cellular subsets involved in this process. This data, in combination with genetic lineage tracing will allow reconstruction of the MuSC lineage hierarchy. We will further characterize cellular subpopulations associated with human muscle dystrophies by performing 3-Dimensional intact-tissue RNA sequencing on patient biopsies The unbiased elucidation of the cellular events underlying the different steps of muscle disease progression at the single-cell level represents crucial missing information, which will push forward our current knowledge on muscle dystrophies. Ultimately, our goal is to develop new biomarkers and eventually new pharmacological approaches to enhance therapy by stimulating intrinsic muscle tissue repair and capitalize on our single cell expertise to uncover disease-related subsets in human biopsies.

column36: Defining and Targeting Autoimmune Liver Disease
column37: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC), a liver autoimmune disease, affects 0.5-1 adults and 0.2 children in 100,000 per year. As a result of the destruction of liver cells during PSC, eventually, many PSC patients will require a liver transplant. The immune system is critical to our health, but much of what is known about the human immune system is derived from animal studies. Since less than 10% of new therapies make it to the clinic, it is critical to develop a better understanding of the human immune system and new models that better predict therapeutic outcomes in humans. A major obstacle to understanding the human immune system is gaining access to healthy human tissues. The surgical team at the Multi-Organ Transplant centre in Toronto modified its liver transplant procedure, which now requires the removal of a small piece of the healthy liver. Using this tissue, we have established a method for isolating the fragile cells from the human liver. Using a new revolutionary technique, single cell RNA sequencing, we generated RNA expression profiles for individual cells obtained from five donated livers. The expression profiles were used to put together the first ever map of the cells that make up the human liver. Using the human healthy liver as a reference, we will generate similar maps from discarded healthy pediatric livers and in both pediatric and adult patients afflicted with PSC. These new maps of PSC patient livers will help identify the immune cells in the liver that contribute and advance PSC pathogenesis. Using these maps, we will address questions about the role of sex (PSC is more prevalent in men) and underlying differences in PSC in children (fast vs. slow progression) vs. PSC in adults. With this knowledge, we aim to identify potential cellular targets and effective therapies for the treatment of autoimmune liver disease.

column36: Improving Family Caregivers' Experiences of Caring for Older Adults with Delirium Superimposed on Dementia in the Acute Care Setting
column37: Approximately half a million Canadians live with dementia. Caring for persons living with dementia (PLWD) can contribute to caregiver distress and strain. Delirium superimposed on dementia (DSD) occurs in 25% of PLWD when they are hospitalized. Delirium is a serious, sudden state of confusion with multiple causes, such as infection or illness. DSD is linked to increased death and complications in PLWD and increased family caregiver distress. Despite the high incidence of DSD among PLWD and the distress it brings to family caregivers, we know little about the experiences of these caregivers in the Canadian healthcare system and their recommendations for change. This proposed qualitative study with an interpretive description approach will enhance understanding of family caregivers' experiences of DSD in hospitalized PLWD. This study plans to determine which elements impact family caregivers' distress during the hospital stay and to identify strategies that decrease caregiver distress. Ten to fifteen family caregivers will be interviewed and data will be analyzed using thematic analysis. It is vitally important to decrease caregiver distress, as it is linked to poor mental and physical health outcomes among family caregivers. Furthermore, studies show only 30-40% of delirium cases are preventable. Maintaining health of caregivers is critical to their ability to continue to care for PLWD in the community. Health care providers have opportunities to engage with family caregivers during their family member's hospitalization and reduce their distress. This study will result in a rich description of the experience of caregivers whose family members are hospitalized with DSD and identify solutions that can be used by healthcare providers to improve their experiences.

column36: A tailored viro-immunotherapy combination approach for the treatment of BRCA1/2 mutated breast and ovarian cancers
column37: BRCA1 and BRCA2 are tumour suppressor genes, both playing essential roles in the DNA repair pathway. Loss of function in either may lead to genetic instability of cells, ultimately leading to malignancy. Alterations (mutations) in either contribute the greatest risk factor for developing breast or ovarian cancer. These cancers tend to be difficult to treat as many do not respond to conventional therapy, while others develop resistance over time. The treatment of BRCA1/2 mutated breast and ovarian cancers with DNA repair inhibitors (commonly known as PARPi) has initially led to promising outcomes. Oral PARPi treatment can selectively kill BRCA1/2 mutated cancer cells through a combination effect targeting the DNA repair pathway. Unfortunately, this treatment is not successful in all patients. Various mechanisms for PARPi resistance have been shown, including restoration of BRCA1/2 function due to differences in the genetic make-up of tumour cells or additional alternations in the BRCA1/2 genes. Oncolytic or "cancer-killing" viruses are an innovative approach to treating even the most complex cancers. Oncolytic viruses target and destroy cancer cells, leaving normal cells unharmed, all while activating a patient's own immune system to fight the cancer. The aim of this project is (1) to engineer cancer specific viruses targeting the BRCA1/2 genes, (2) evaluate the combination effect of these engineered BRCA1/2 targeting viruses with PARPi, and finally (3) complete a pre-clinical evaluation of BRCA1/2 targeting viruses with PARPi therapy including safety and efficacy using a variety of mouse models. The goal of this project is to develop a combination therapy that can overcome drug resistance and lead to curative treatment for patients with BRCA1/2 mutated cancers.

column36: Machine learning-based identification of diagnostic biomarkers in prostate cancer with intraductal carcinoma.
column37: Prostate cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer among Canadian men. When diagnosed with prostate cancer, patients are classified in different risk categories for recurrence of the cancer after treatment. This classification guides the type of treatment that the patient will receive after diagnosis. For example, a prostate cancer patient exhibiting a high risk of recurrence will typically receive a more aggressive treatment than one with a lower risk. These individualized treatment options result in a better prognosis of the disease. However, not all known risk factors of recurrence are currently used in prostate cancer recurrence risk stratification. The presence of tumour growth in the ducts of the prostate is one of those factors that increases the risk of recurrence. However, due to their small size, these tumour growths are often missed in tumour biopsies and patients are therefore not treated appropriately. In this project, I propose to use a technology named imaging mass spectrometry that allows the identification of molecules in very small regions of the prostate. The detection of these molecules can then be used to determine the presence of tumour growth in prostate ducts and provide patients with the appropriate treatment. I will also use a computational and statistical approach that will identify the set of molecules that provide the most accurate prediction of the presence of tumour growth in prostate cancer. The discovered molecules will make the diagnosis of prostate cancer more accurate and ensure that the treatment of patients is more tailored to their condition. Ultimately, my project will reduce prostate cancer recurrence and improve its survival rate.

column36: Investigating Suicidal Behaviour in Adolescent Males and Females Using Functional Imaging
column37: Major depressive disorder (MDD), anxiety and suicide-related outcomes are highly comorbid in adolescent populations. Failed prevention efforts corresponding to escalating suicide rates may be associated with lack of knowledge regarding the progression from suicidal ideation (SI) to suicide attempts (SA). In addition, impulsivity in adolescence may significantly contribute to this progression. Functional neuroimaging correlates of SI, SA and impulsivity may provide insight into who is most at risk for attempts, however, this is understudied in adolescent cohorts. In addition, important gender differences in neural correlates and clinical measures of suicidality may exist, which may require different strategies for diagnosis and treatment. The objectives of this study are: 1) To classify the progression from SI to SA in adolescents using functional connectivity data; 2) To examine the role of impulsivity as a risk factor for suicide attempts; 3) To determine if neural correlates of SI, SA and impulsivity differ between male and female subjects. This study will thus identify those at highest risk of suicide attempts in an adolescent cohort, allowing for implementation of more timely and effective interventional strategies.

column36: For Improving diagnostics and grasping the disease mechanisms of rare hypomagnesemia in patients with CNNM2 mutations
column37: Low blood magnesium (hypomagnesemia) is a common electrolyte disorder that causes fatigue, muscle cramps, and arrhythmias. The CNNM2 gene encodes a protein that is responsible for the transport of magnesium in the kidney, the primary organ responsible for maintaining magnesium balance through urinary excretion. Our collaborators have previously described patient mutations in the CNNM2 gene that are causative of hypomagnesemia and that the activity of CNNM2 may be directly dependent on its interaction with other factors. Therefore, in this multidisciplinary grant proposal, my group plans to specifically address the question of which factors can interact with CNNM2. We will use various biochemical approaches to identify such partners and how they affect CNNM2 function, including its magnesium transport ability in kidney cells. We believe that uncovering the determinants of CNNM2 function will provide us with a landscape of the physiological mechanism by which CNNM2 regulates magnesium levels. This information would then be employed to investigate potential changes in CNNM2 function induced by the patient mutations, guide future therapeutic development, and provide other means to mitigate the severity of CNNM2 associated diseases.

column36: Evaluating Burden of Care for Caregivers of Children with Intestinal Failure on Long-Term Parenteral Nutrition
column37: Intestinal failure (IF) is a complex medical condition resulting in malabsorption of fluids and nutrients that requires partial or total parenteral nutrition (PN) support to sustain growth and hydration. I Pediatric intestinal failure (PIF) is caused by short bowel syndrome (SBS), dysmotility disorders and mucosal enteropathies. IF is often further compounded by additional nutritional, infectious and metabolic complications. With improved survival rates, more patients are receiving intensive management within the home setting that includes PN, enteral nutrition therapy, medications, as well as, devices such as feeding tubes, stomas and central venous catheters. Few studies have discussed the impact of highly specialized medical care on caregivers as most pediatric IF patients are unable to provide their own care due to their young age at diagnosis. Caring for a child with IF on home PN requires significant training and continued hypervigilence for years and potentially life long. Anecdotally, parents report significant strain on finances, relationships and individual/family functioning. Families also receive minimal, if any, home care support as they are considered fully trained to provide the care required and do not qualify for most resources. Currently, there are no publications on the burden of care for caregivers of children on home PN. The goal of this research project is to determine the effects of caring for a child with intestinal failure on long-term PN on the caregivers. Through the evaluation of their quality of life, informal care and sleep we can better understand the burden of care on the caregivers, including overall mental and physical well-being, financial and social. Further evaluation of what supports they currently have access to and what gaps exist will allow us to advocate for resources and supports in the areas that families need them to preserve this valuable commodity.

column36: Knowledge to Action: Exploring Referral Patterns and Physiotherapy Management of Stress Urinary Incontinence in Women in Ontario
column37: The prevalence of urinary incontinence (UI) is high in Canada and increases with age, affecting 16% of women under 40 years old and 55% of women greater than 65 years old. Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) is the involuntary loss of urine during a cough, sneeze or any type of exertion, and accounts for 50% of UI cases. SUI leads to reduced health-related quality of life and places a multi-billion dollar burden on the health care system each year. Supervised intensive pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT), delivered by trained pelvic floor physiotherapists (PTs), is an effective treatment for SUI in women and is therefore recommended as first line management by Canadian Clinical Practice Guidelines. Despite the existence of an effective treatment, SUI continues to be a widespread problem. It is unknown whether this stems from the lack of referral to pelvic floor PTs for PFMT services or the inadequate application of SUI treatment in clinical practice among pelvic floor PTs. The ultimate goal of my research is to improve the delivery of effective care for women with SUI in Ontario. As such, I aim to evaluate the current referral and treatment practices for the management of SUI in women and to understand the barriers to providing effective treatment in both rural and urban settings. By consulting with key stakeholders (pelvic floor PTs and primary referral sources) I will be able to design a specific strategy to improve SUI treatment for Ontario women and thus mitigate the devastating personal and economic consequences of the condition.

column36: Perinatal maternal opioid use: Exploring prescribing trends, and the maternal and neonatal safety of postpartum opioids using administrative data
column37: Opioids, such as codeine, morphine, oxycodone, and fentanyl are drugs used for the treatment of pain. The prescribing of opioids has increased dramatically over the past two decades. While the majority of opioid prescriptions are well intentioned, they are often prescribed in larger quantities, for far longer than intended, which has led to the genesis and propagation of the opioid epidemic. One area of this epidemic that has been less well explored is the prescription of opioids to women following childbirth. Over 15,000 Ontario women a year are newly started on opioids following the birth of a child. My doctoral thesis will use large healthcare databases to examine the maternal and child health consequences associated with the prescription of opioids to mothers following childbirth. We plan to conduct three interrelated studies that focus around this central theme. The first study will examine trends in opioid prescribing to women after birth of a child in Ontario. A high profile case report published in 2006 described the potential harm of codeine use during breastfeeding. This report may have led to an overall decrease in codeine use, and an increase in oxycodone use among new mothers. This is of concern because oxycodone is a far stronger opioid drug with a greater potential for long-term abuse and dependence. The second study will examine whether oxycodone use is a risk factor for persistent maternal opioid use following childbirth. We believe there is a greater risk of long-term opioid use in mothers prescribed oxycodone, compared to codeine. The final study will examine the risks to babies associated with maternal opioid use following childbirth. Many clinicians believe that breastfeeding newborns are at risk of harm from opioids ingested via breast milk. We will assess whether there is an increased risk of harm in newborns whose mothers received an opioid prescription relative to those whose mothers did not.

column36: A Cross-Study Data Analytic Approach to Identifying Neuroanatomical Signatures of Anxiety in Neurodevelopmental Disorders
column37: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) are a common class of disorders characterized by impairment of the development of the central nervous system. Such disorders often co-occur with additional psychiatric conditions that have a negative impact on the quality of life of patients. In particular, anxiety is a comorbidity that is not well understood in this sub-population. No established treatment pathways exist by which clinicians can aid children and youth with neurodevelopmental disorders who also suffer from anxiety. The identification and development of potentially effective novel treatments calls for a deeper understanding of the neuroscience that underlies this comorbidity. As a first step towards teasing out the neurobiology underlying the condition, data from neuroimaging studies can be used to discern which brain regions play a role in anxiety within the context of NDDs. To that end, I plan to analyze the data from three separate preclinical and clinical neuroimaging studies of neurodevelopmental disorders with the goal of identifying a convergent neuroanatomical signature of comorbid anxiety. A preliminary analysis of data from one of the studies has hinted at the potential implication of a number of structures, including the cerebellum, hippocampus and amygdala. The neuroanatomical signature identified following the analysis of all three data sets can ultimately be used as the basis for subsequent inquiries into the underlying neurobiological mechanisms.

column36: Improving internet-delivered cognitive behavioural therapy: Including insomnia treatment in transdiagnostic therapy for anxiety and depression to maximize patient benefit.
column37: One in five Canadians will meet criteria for an anxiety or depression disorder in their lifetime. Anxiety and depression can be debilitating and these disorders produce a large economic cost and present significant challenges for our health care systems. Cognitive behavioural therapy has been shown to produce long-lasting reductions in anxiety and depression symptoms, but patients face significant barriers to accessing face-to-face psychotherapy, such as high costs, long travel distances, and scheduling difficulties. New transdiagnostic programs eliminate many barriers by offering therapy online and have been shown to reduce symptoms by 50% on average; however, one quarter of patients do not complete treatment and another quarter do not report significant benefit. To improve treatment outcomes for these clients, I examined the primary concerns reported by previous patients who received anxiety and depression therapy. The most common concern, reported by 75% of patients, was sleep disruption. Sleep problems are known to play a role in the development of depression. In fact, research shows that insomnia often precedes a depressive episode. Insomnia appears to play such an important role in depression that online treatments that only address insomnia produce reductions in depression symptoms. Despite this evidence, transdiagnostic therapies for anxiety and depression do not focus on sleep. I propose that a new sleep-enhanced transdiagnostic protocol be developed and then tested in a randomized trial. The sleep-enhanced program is expected to produce greater reductions in symptoms and could also increase completion rates. The improved program will then be available to the public through the Online Therapy Unit, which provides free therapy online to over 1000 patients in Saskatchewan each year. Results will be published in order to inform other practitioners of internet-delivered therapy about the importance of sleep in treatment for anxiety and depression.

column36: Investigating a biological specificity conundrum: the role of dynamics in transcription factor binding
column37: Transcription factors (TF) are proteins that bind specific regions of our DNA and thereby turn genes on/off. Many diseases, including cancers, are caused by misregulation of gene expression, so fully understanding how a TF functions is key to understanding disease progression. The three-dimensional structures (conformations) of many TFs are known, allowing for limited predictions regarding how these proteins recognize the DNA sequences of the genes that they regulate. However, some of the most important genes controlled by a TF have sequences that do not fit these consensus predictions. One possible explanation for this apparent anomaly is that proteins are very flexible and can easily adopt alternative shapes that are capable of binding variant DNA sequences. The goal of my research is to test this hypothesized explanation by studying how the ensemble of conformations that an individual TF can adopt affects its ability to bind DNA. Starting with a model TF called ETV6, I will use the tools of protein engineering to create mutants that are more flexible than the normal form found in our cells. A more flexible protein can rapidly interconvert between many different shapes, whereas an inflexible protein persists in fewer conformations. I predict that the additional conformations adoptable by the ETV6 mutants will assist in binding non-consensus DNA sequences. To test this prediction, I will use high-throughput methods to compare the DNA-binding preferences of the mutant versus parental forms of ETV6, and to quantitatively measure the strengths of their binding interactions. Through these investigations, I will be able to show how the flexibility of a TF influences the set of genes that it controls. This will help us diagnosis how aberrant TFs can lead to diseases and may lead to new therapies to manipulate their conformations and thereby dictate how they regulate gene expression.

column36: Development of CAR-T cells targeting WT1 peptide presented by HLA class II molecules
column37: Immunotherapy is a type of cancer treatment that strengthens body's immune system against cancer cells. Among various forms of immunotherapy, adoptive T cell therapy is a promising and well-established approach. It involves isolation of immune cells from patients, especially T cells, which are then genetically modified to express tumor-specific receptors prior to re-infusion back into patients. For instance, T cells can be engineered to express tumor-specific CAR (chimeric antigen receptor). Importantly, CAR-T cell therapy has been shown to induce remarkable clinical responses in some patients with leukemia. WT1 (Wilms Tumour 1) is a protein which is over-expressed in tumour cells compared to normal cells. Strategies targeting WT1-expressing tumour cells have been developed; however, so far these strategies can only be applied to certain subsets of patients with compatible gene types. Here, we aim to develop WT1-specific CAR-T cell therapy which targets WT1 protein in an unique manner in order to target WT1-expressing tumour cells from patients with a variety of gene types. In addition, our strategy can also be applied to other tumour-related proteins, hence it can benefit numerous patients with different types of cancer.
